name: Base colour textures
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

## Parent

nc3cv6do (Milestone 12: packs, textures and PBR). Read its spec first.

## What to build

A mesh draws its glTF base colour texture. Vertex gains uv; there is one vertex format and one pipeline. The loader reads TEXCOORD_0, the base colour texture (PNG from the GLB binary chunk) and its sampler: nearest or linear, wrap, mipmaps when the minification filter asks. Images upload as SRGB8A8; mipmaps are built on the CPU with a 2x2 box filter in linear light. A mesh with no texture binds a 1x1 white image. The primitives get UVs. baseColorFactor stays in the vertex colour and multiplies the texture. A JPEG texture is skipped with a log. Demo: make_meshes.py gives Kula's face.glb a simple bordered texture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] glTF tests with built GLB bytes: UVs read; an embedded PNG and its sampler read; a JPEG skipped with a log; a mesh with no texture uses the white image.
- [ ] Image tests: mipmap sizes and linear-light values for a known image.
- [ ] Every primitive has UVs.
- [ ] Kula draws the textured face; the other games draw as before.

## Blocked by

- jw0tlmqt
result: Meshes draw their glTF base colour texture through one uv vertex format and pipeline, with sampler, sRGB upload, linear-light CPU mipmaps and a white image fallback. Kula's face is textured.

commit.message: feat(textures): Draw the glTF base colour texture - Vertex gains uv. One vertex format and one pipeline. Every primitive has uvs, and a mesh with no texture binds a 1x1 white image. - The loader reads TEXCOORD_0, the embedded PNG base colour texture and its sampler. A JPEG, a bad PNG or mixed textures log once and the mesh still loads. - Images upload as SRGB8A8. Mipmaps are built on the CPU with a 2x2 box filter in linear light when the min filter asks. - baseColorFactor stays in the vertex colour and multiplies the texture. - make_meshes.py gives Kula's face.glb a bordered texture.

name: Kula: keep the ball spinning during a jump and a fall
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: task

## What happens

The ball spins only while it rolls. Ball.advance_motion changes rot only in Rolling. During Jumping, JumpingInPlace and Falling the ball is frozen in the air, which looks wrong after a fast roll. The test 'Ball.advance(Ball.act(floor_ahead, still, forward_jump), 0.54).rot == Quat.identity' in games/kula/Ball.roc records this.

## What the original does

Read in kula-world-decomp at 2ca79ff, src/player_movement.c. rotX is the spin rate. SetBallShapeAndRotationWhenJumping applies it with RotMatrixX(rotX * -6).
- A forward jump sets rotX to VELOCITY(40), the top roll speed, when it starts (:204).
- A jump in place sets rotX to 0 each frame (:456).
- FALLING raises rotX by 6 a frame, up to 40, when the ball was rolling forward. Otherwise rotX drops by 1 a frame to 0 (:414-424).
- ROLLING sets rotX to movementVelocity (:316).

Check one thing first. Does RotMatrixX build a per-frame step or the full angle? This decides whether rotX is a rate.

## Expected

- A forward jump spins about the right axis at the top roll rate, 1 cell per 0.26 s over Ball.radius.
- A jump in place does not spin.
- A fall keeps or builds the spin, as above.
- The spin carries on into the next roll with no jump in angle.

## Done when

- SPEC.md 'Spin' row states the original's rule, with a Code label.
- Ball tests cover the spin for each motion. The old identity test changes.

Found during 86idkndt.
result: Jump and fall spin match the original's rotX rule. rotX is a rate (RotMatrixX accumulates into matrix_254). Forward jump: top roll rate. Jump in place: none. Fall: arc keeps the rate, drop builds to top with Up held, else stops in 0.8 s. SPEC.md Spin row updated with a Code label.

commit.message: fix(kula): Keep the ball spinning during a jump and a fall

name: Compute contacts on the host: sweep and prune, then box and sphere tests
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

New engine/collision.odin with tests. The host computes contacts from the current Scene's colliders after view and hands them to the next step.

- World AABB per collider from kind, pos, yaw and extent. Unknown kind: log once per run and skip.
- Broadphase: sweep and prune on x. Sort by AABB min x on the frame arena each step, then scan.
- Narrowphase: box-box by separating axis on five axes (y and the two ground-plane axes of each box), sphere-sphere, box-sphere. Boxes honour yaw.
- One contact per pair, a < b, normal from a to b on the least-overlap axis, depth is the overlap. Sort by (a, b).
- Duplicate ids: first wins, log once per run.
- The contact list crosses the seam as a Roc list. Empty means no allocation.
- Odin tests: each pair test, the broadphase, the sort order, the duplicate log, the unknown kind, and a timing at 1,000 colliders. Record the time in docs/DESIGN.md section 10.

Decisions: docs/ROADMAP.md, Milestone 6. Part of 'Milestone 6: collision as data'.
result: engine/collision.odin computes contacts after view; the next step gets them. 80 Odin tests pass. host-check and alloc-check pass on arm64mac and in the Linux image. 1,000 colliders: about 1.3 ms under -debug, 230 us under -o:speed. x64win not checked.

commit.message: feat(engine): Compute contacts on the host from the Scene colliders - engine/collision.odin finds contacts with a sweep and prune on x, then box-box, sphere-sphere and box-sphere tests. - Contacts have a < b, a normal from a to b and the overlap depth, sorted by (a, b). - Duplicate ids and unknown kinds are skipped and logged once per run. - The Seam computes contacts after view, so the next step gets them. - DESIGN.md records the search and its time at 1,000 colliders.

name: The step rate from Launch
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Parent

Milestone 17: Launch (nm2ai3l5). Read it with `dex show nm2ai3l5 --full`. ADR 0007 and the CONTEXT.md entries for `launch` and Launch bind the design.

## What to build

The clock takes `step_hz` at init and keeps the fixed interval as a field.
`dt` to `step` is one over `step_hz`. Lockstep adds one interval per Frame.
The Headless frame duration is the interval. The maximum Frame time stays a
host constant. The Launch check gains `step_hz`: zero is bad. The constant
`FIXED_DT` leaves the engine, except as the default's value in the Launch
module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Frame tests at a non-default `step_hz`, such as 60, check one step per
interval in real-clock mode, one step per Frame in Lockstep, and that
`step` sees a `dt` of one over 60.
- [ ] The existing frame tests at 120 Hz keep their meaning.
- [ ] The Launch check table test gains the `step_hz` row.
- [ ] Manual check: pong with a 60 Hz Launch plays at the same speed, because
pong scales by `dt`.
- [ ] `scripts/test-all.sh` passes, including the Spans build.

## Blocked by

- zcqzpfck
result: The clock takes step_hz at init and keeps fixed_dt as a field; step sees a dt of one over step_hz. Lockstep adds one interval per Frame and the Headless platform reads the clock's interval. The host inits the clock from the checked Launch before init. launch_check names step_hz at zero. FIXED_DT left the engine; the default stays 120 in launch_default and pf.Launch.default. Frame tests at 60 Hz cover the real clock, Lockstep and Headless. For 8log5tcb: docs/DESIGN.md lines 35, 92 and 806 still say 120 Hz as a host fact, and docs/RESEARCH-SCALING.md line 49 still lists FIXED_DT.

name: Milestone 19: the Bridge
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

A script, a CI test or an agent cannot play a rocco game. CI runs each game
for one Frame with no input and checks only the exit code.
`scripts/screenshot.sh` works on macOS only, needs the Screen Recording
permission, and captures after a wall-clock delay, so two runs differ. An
agent that changes a game cannot press a key, read where an entity is, or
see the result of N steps.

## Solution

The Bridge: a host module that lets one Driver control a run over a
localhost socket. The Driver injects Input, asks for fixed steps, reads the
Scene as JSON and saves a screenshot. Under the Bridge, Lockstep pauses, so
the same requests always give the same Scenes. The game does not know the
Bridge exists.

Done when a Driver plays a game over a localhost socket in Lockstep. It
injects Input for N steps, reads the Scene as JSON and saves a screenshot.

Check: in CI on Linux (xvfb) and macOS, `scripts/bridge.py` runs tutorial
chapter 3, holds W for 30 steps, asserts that Pip's Draw moved by the
expected distance, and saves a screenshot with the window's size.

## Decisions (grilled 2026-10-22)

- Scope: the Bridge only. Ports (`Tell`, `Ask`, `Listen`) wait for the
  extension arc. No Vocabulary change. ADR 0009 records this.
- Terms: **Bridge** and **Driver** are in CONTEXT.md. "bridge" stays under
  _Avoid_ for Seam. The Lockstep entry says it pauses under the Bridge.
- Room for Ports: the socket and the JSON Lines framing are one host
  module; the Driver ops are another. The ops `tell`, `ask` and `listen`
  are reserved and reply `"error":"not yet"`.
- Switch: `ROCCO_BRIDGE=<port>`. The host listens on TCP 127.0.0.1 only and
  accepts one Driver at a time. The Bridge is compiled into every build,
  release builds included.
- Clock: a Bridge run is Lockstep that pauses. It runs one fixed step per
  Frame while the Driver owes steps, and zero steps when none are owed. The
  window renders every Frame. No new Run_Mode term.
- Threads: none. The host polls the socket non-blocking once per Frame on
  the main thread. Neither link catalog has `pthread_create`.
- Headless: the host blocks on the socket while no steps are owed. With
  `ROCCO_BRIDGE`, Headless does not need `ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES`.
- Lifecycle: the host runs `launch` and `init`, opens the window, shows the
  first `view`, and waits with zero steps for a Driver. When the Driver
  disconnects, the host waits for the next one. If the port is in use, the
  host exits with an error and does not start a normal run.
- Real devices: while the Bridge is on, the host ignores the real keyboard
  and mouse for `step`. The debug camera stays host-only and still works.
- Wire format: JSON Lines. One request object per line, one reply object
  per line. Every reply has `ok`; a failed one also has `error`.
- Ops:
  - `hello`: the protocol version, the step rate, the step count, and
    Headless or windowed.
  - `step`: `n`, `held`, `tap`, `mouse`. Reply: the step count after the N
    steps, the Commands the game returned in those steps, and the alloc
    line fields of the last step.
  - `scene`: the current Scene as JSON, with the Vocabulary's field and tag
    names, plus the QueryResults that the next `step` gets.
  - `screenshot`: `path`. Reply: the path, the physical size and the
    logical size. Headless replies with an error.
  - `quit`: reply `ok`, then end the run as a `Quit` Command does.
- Input in `step`: `held` is a list of Key names from `pf.Key`, held for
  all N steps. The host derives Pressed from the `held` of the step before,
  as the real latch does. `tap` keys are Pressed but not Held, in the first
  step only. `mouse` is `[dx, dy]`, in the first step only. An absent
  `held` means no key is held. The Key names come from the same table that
  generates `platform/Key.roc`.
- Render while paused: the Frame render pairs the current Scene with
  itself, so the window and a screenshot show what `scene` returns. Today
  Lockstep's Alpha is always 0, so it draws the previous Scene.
- Screenshot: the host renders each Frame to an offscreen target and copies
  it to the swapchain. A screenshot reads the target back with a native
  copy per backend: Metal `getBytes`, a D3D11 staging texture, GL
  `glReadPixels`. A hand-written PNG writer with stored deflate blocks, a
  CRC32 and an Adler-32 writes physical pixels. No new link input. ADR 0010
  records this.
- Link catalog: Windows gains a `ws2_32` import library. The macOS sysroot
  gains the socket symbols that `core:sys/posix` needs. Linux `core:net`
  makes raw syscalls and needs no new stubs.
- Drivers: `scripts/bridge.py`, Python standard library only, is a library
  and a CLI. Each CLI call connects, sends one request, prints the reply
  and disconnects, so an agent can drive a run across Bash calls.
  `scripts/screenshot.sh` keeps its arguments but drives the Bridge; its
  third argument becomes a step count. `scripts/macos/wincap.swift` is
  deleted.
- Docs: a new guide page, `guide/bridge.md`, in plain prose. The running
  and debugging page links to it. `docs/NOTES.md` marks the
  `ROCCO_INPUT_SCRIPT` note as superseded by the Bridge.

## Out of scope

- Ports, and any message from the Driver to the game.
- Golden-image comparison. The CI check asserts the screenshot's size only.
- Driving a spawn step in `scripts/alloc-check.sh` (its own task).
- Connections from other machines.

## Tasks in order

1. indftha8: Prefactor: render to an offscreen target (any time).
2. hfgw7tnb: Bridge transport, hello and quit (tracer bullet, any time).
3. hvpxyd98: The step op (after 2).
4. 0gsffuak: The scene op (after 3).
5. h1boef83: The screenshot op (after 1 and 3; parallel with 4).
6. 9d9sz243: Drivers: bridge.py, screenshot.sh and the CI check (after 4 and 5).
7. tazwh2dr: Finish the Bridge docs (after 6).

Outside the milestone: tijkhm82, the alloc-check spawn step (after 6).
result:
A Driver plays a game over a localhost socket in Lockstep. ROCCO_BRIDGE=<port> turns on the Bridge with the ops hello, step, scene, screenshot and quit. scripts/bridge.py is the Driver, and scripts/screenshot.sh drives the Bridge on all three targets. guide/bridge.md documents the protocol.

Done check: scripts/bridge_check.py holds W for 30 steps in tutorial chapter 3, checks that Pip moved -0.625 along z and saves a screenshot with the window's size. It passed in CI on Linux (xvfb), macOS and Windows: https://github.com/Pixelsprout/rocco-engine/actions/runs/39686103853

name: Kula skeleton: games/kula in the scripts, World, Grid, Level and a drawn level
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

The Kula skeleton: the game exists, the scripts know it, and the engine
draws a parsed level with a fixed camera. See the decisions in Milestone 10
(72omk38x). Grilled 2026-10-13.

## Requirements

Scripts:
1. In scripts/build.roc, `game <name>` resolves `games/<name>` first, then
`examples/<name>`. Add Game("kula") to "all". Update the expects.
2. Add `game kula` to scripts/host-check.sh and `kula` to the game loop in
scripts/linux/in-container.sh. Leave scripts/alloc-check.sh alone.
3. Add `games/*/*.bin`, `.exe`, `.pdb`, `.lib` lines to .gitignore.

Modules, all under games/kula/, each a type module beside main.roc:
4. World.roc holds the types: `Cell : { x : I32, y : I32, z : I32 }`, an axis
is a Cell with one component of magnitude 1, `Pose : { cell : Cell, up : Cell,
forward : Cell }`, `Item : [Key, Exit]`, `Level : { blocks : Set(Cell), items
: List({ cell : Cell, item : Item }), start : Pose }`, and `Model`.
5. Grid.roc holds cell arithmetic: add, sub, neg, cross, scale by I32, and
`has_block : Set(Cell), Cell -> Bool`. Each has an expect.
6. Level.roc has `import "levels/level1.txt" as level1 : Str` at the top of
the file, above the type module line. `parse : Str -> Try(Level,
[RaggedRow(U64), UnknownChar(Str), NoStart, TwoStarts])`. Layers are
separated by a blank line, bottom layer first. Row index is z, column index
is x, layer index is y. `.` empty, `#` block, `S` block with the ball on its
top face, `K` block with a key on its top face, `E` block with the exit on
its top face. The start pose is the cell above the S block, up +y, forward
-z. Expects cover the parse of level1, the start pose, each item cell, and
each error.
7. levels/level1.txt is the smallest map that forces one straight run, one
wall climb, one edge roll onto a block's side, one gap jump, two keys and
the exit. Two layers, under 12 cells wide. Write the intended route as a
comment in the Level expects, not in the file.
8. main.roc has the header with pf and linalg, `init` that parses level1
and crashes on Err, `step` that returns the model and `Quit` on an Escape
press, and `view` that draws every block as the primitive cube with a tint,
keys as 0.3 gold cubes hovering half a cell above the face, the exit block
in its own tint, and the ball as the primitive sphere at the start pose.
Camera is a fixed look-at over the level with up +y. cursor is Free.
colliders is empty.
9. Imports point downward only: main -> Level -> Grid -> World.

## Not in scope

- No movement, no input other than Escape, no rules.
- No .glb meshes yet.
- No README yet.

## Done when

- `roc test games/kula/main.roc` passes.
- `roc scripts/build.roc -- game kula` builds and the level is visible on
arm64mac.
- scripts/host-check.sh passes.
result: games/kula draws level1 with a fixed camera. Scripts resolve games/ first. The level is one cell wide. A jump onto the block ahead can skip the wall climb.

name: The capacities from Launch
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Parent

Milestone 17: Launch (nm2ai3l5). Read it with `dex show nm2ai3l5 --full`. ADR 0007 and the CONTEXT.md entries for `launch` and Launch bind the design.

## What to build

The mesh table, the sky table and the Pack reference arrays become slices
allocated once from the permanent allocator at the Launch's capacity. The
frame render's placed list and pairing map reserve `draws`. The UI quads
take `ui_quads`, which the UI init already accepts. The uniform buffer size
follows `draws`. The texture pool follows `meshes` and `skies`. The UI
element count stays a Clay constant. Past a capacity at run time the host
keeps today's rule: log once, draw the first N. The Launch check gains the
capacity rules: a zero in any capacity, `ui_quads` past 16,384 (the u16
index bound), `meshes` below four (the Fallback mesh and the three
Primitives) and `skies` below two (the reserved slot and one sky). The
Draws and Mixed bench games set `draws` from the N Arg through the shared
bench helpers and fall back to the default when N is missing, because
`init` already stops the run on a bad N. The constants `MESH_CAPACITY`,
`SKY_CAPACITY`, `DRAW_CAPACITY`, `PAIRING_CAPACITY` and `UI_QUAD_CAPACITY`
leave the engine, except as the default's values in the Launch module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mesh table, sky table and Pack tests construct their tables at a small
capacity and check the full-table result at that capacity.
- [ ] Frame render tests at a small `draws` check log-once-and-drop at that
capacity and that the pairing map reserves it.
- [ ] The Launch check table test gains the capacity rows.
- [ ] The Draws bench game at N 16,384 runs Headless as before. The golden
files of the Model size and Colliders bench games do not change.
- [ ] `scripts/test-all.sh`, `scripts/host-check.sh`, `scripts/alloc-check.sh`
and `bench/check.sh` pass.

## Blocked by

- zcqzpfck
result:
The mesh table, the sky table and the Pack refs are slices from the permanent allocator at the Launch's capacity. The frame render's placed list, draw cap and pairing map take draws, and the UI quads take ui_quads. The sokol image, sampler and view pools follow meshes and skies, and the uniform buffer follows draws. The view pool is now set, because sokol's default of 256 would overflow at a large meshes capacity.

packs_init lists the asset names that launch's Config needs, and packs_attach sizes the refs after launch. The Launch check names the field and the rule. It rejects a zero capacity, ui_quads past 16384, meshes below 4 and skies below 2. It also rejects meshes or skies past 65536, because an id packs its slot in 16 bits, and draws past 2796197, because sokol takes the uniform buffer size as a C int. Those two bounds were not in the spec. The review added them, because without them a typo crashes on an assert or wraps the buffer size.

The Draws and Mixed bench games set draws from N through Bench.draws_for_n. The Draws bench game ran Headless at N 16384 for 2120 frames, and at N 20000 with no drop message. The golden files did not change. test-all.sh, host-check.sh, alloc-check.sh and bench/check.sh pass. The five capacity constants are gone from the engine. docs/BENCHMARKS.md and docs/RESEARCH-SCALING.md still name them; 8log5tcb owns the docs.

name: Fix GL clip-space depth with sokol-shdc fixup_clipspace
description:
Add '@glsl_options fixup_clipspace' to the @vs block in engine/shaders/basic.glsl and regenerate engine/shader_basic.odin with the command in its header.

Why: the projection in engine/math.odin (mat4_perspective_reversed_infinite) produces Metal and D3D11 style clip depth, z_clip in [0, w]. GL expects [-w, w]. sokol's GL backend never calls glClipControl, so on Linux the depth buffer holds 0.5 + near/(2d) instead of near/d. Ordering stays correct, so the picture looks right, but the reversed-Z precision is gone and far objects z-fight. The shdc option rewrites gl_Position.z in the GLSL output only. Metal and HLSL output are untouched. This keeps the projection and the pipeline desc backend-neutral, which is the rule for milestone 1: clip-space differences are resolved in the shader source, never in Odin.

Rejected alternative: glClipControl(GL_LOWER_LEFT, GL_ZERO_TO_ONE) from platform_linux.odin. Needs a GL function loader in Odin and GL 4.5.

Steps:
1. Add '@glsl_options fixup_clipspace' as the first line inside '@vs vs'.
2. Regenerate with sokol-shdc (command in the README and the generated header).
3. Confirm the GLSL 430 block in the generated file gains a gl_Position.z rewrite and the MSL and HLSL blocks are unchanged apart from that.
4. Build on macOS with -vet -strict-style and run examples/bodies: no sokol errors, same picture.
5. Run ./scripts/linux/check.sh: process runs under xvfb.

Done when the generated GLSL contains the clip-space rewrite, macOS still renders, and the Linux check passes. Record in the result the exact generated line.

Part of 'Milestone 1: one source tree, three desktop targets'. Found while reviewing how the pipeline desc behaves across backends: sokol maps face_winding, cull_mode and depth compare per backend, but not clip-space depth.
result: Added '@glsl_options fixup_clipspace' to @vs vs in engine/shaders/basic.glsl and regenerated engine/shader_basic.odin with sokol-shdc 11d0cf6. Generated GLSL 430 line: 'gl_Position.z = 2.0 * gl_Position.z - gl_Position.w;'. MSL and HLSL sources are byte-identical. macOS: host builds with -vet -strict-style, bodies runs with no sokol errors. Linux: ./scripts/linux/check.sh exit 0, process ran under xvfb to the timeout. Correction to the rationale: GL window depth now equals near/d, the same as Metal and D3D11, so depth values match across backends. The fixup does not restore float reversed-Z precision: GL still computes (ndc+1)/2 with ndc near -1 for far objects, and the default depth buffer is probably 24-bit unorm. That precision needs glClipControl(ZERO_TO_ONE) and a D32F target.

commit.message: fix(shader): Remap clip-space z for GL with fixup_clipspace

name: Milestone 12: packs, textures and PBR
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Done when a Pack unloads and the next loads with no stale id drawn, and Kula plays three textured, sky-lit levels with no magenta.

Decided in the Milestone 12 grilling on 2026-10-14. Pong is out of scope (ntbh6adj). The Kula look is in games/kula/SPEC.md (Look).

## Problem Statement

A game cannot change what is loaded while it runs. The host loads every mesh in assets/meshes/ once, before init, and keeps it for the whole run. Kula needs a different block set and sky for each Theme. A larger game needs to stream content in and out. The engine also draws only vertex colours with Lambert light: no textures, no sky, no specular. The Kula look in SPEC.md needs all three.

## Solution

The engine gains the Pack: a named set of assets that load and unload together. A game sends Load with a pack name and a list of asset names, and the host calls the new seam function loaded with the ids. The game sends Unload when it is done with a pack. "Level" becomes a game word; the engine has no level.

The renderer reads glTF base colour textures and metallic-roughness materials and lights them with a GGX BRDF. A Scene can name a cubemap sky. Kula uses one pack per Theme, swaps packs between three levels, and draws textured blocks under a Theme sky.

## User Stories

1. As a game author, I want to name the assets a pack holds in Roc, so that my game data decides what loads together.
2. As a game author, I want to load a pack with a Command, so that I can change content while the game runs.
3. As a game author, I want to unload a pack by name, so that memory frees when I no longer need its assets.
4. As a game author, I want several packs loaded at once, so that a world pack and a room pack can live together.
5. As a game author, I want to unload packs in any order, so that streamed chunks behind the player can go first.
6. As a game author, I want an asset named by two packs to load once and keep one id, so that shared assets cost nothing extra.
7. As a game author, I want a shared asset to stay loaded until its last pack unloads, so that unloading one pack never breaks another.
8. As a game author, I want loaded called with the pack name and its manifest, so that I know exactly when ids exist.
9. As a game author, I want loaded to run before the next view, so that a swap never draws a stale id.
10. As a game author, I want every name I asked for to appear in the manifest, so that I always get an answer.
11. As a game author, I want a missing or broken asset to get id 0 and one log line, so that a typo is visible, not fatal.
12. As a game author, I want init to return Commands, so that I can load my first pack before the first step.
13. As a game author, I want Config to list the asset names found on disk, so that I can check names in init.
14. As a game author, I want a Load for a loaded pack to log once and do nothing, so that a repeated Command is harmless.
15. As a game author, I want an Unload for an unknown pack to log once and do nothing, so that a stray Command is harmless.
16. As a game author, I want assets organised by type on disk, not by pack, so that one file can serve many packs.
17. As a game author, I want a stale id to draw the fallback, so that a bug shows as magenta instead of the wrong mesh.
18. As a game author, I want the primitives available with no pack, so that a game can draw before any load.
19. As an artist, I want the glTF base colour texture drawn, so that my Blender materials show in game.
20. As an artist, I want the glTF sampler honoured (nearest or linear, wrap, mipmaps), so that pixel art stays sharp and distant surfaces do not shimmer.
21. As an artist, I want base colour textures treated as sRGB, so that colours match Blender.
22. As an artist, I want baseColorFactor to multiply the texture, so that glTF materials combine as the spec says.
23. As an artist, I want roughness and metallic factors and the metallic-roughness texture read, so that shiny and matte parts look right.
24. As an artist, I want a mesh with no material to stay matte grey, so that primitives and plain meshes never turn into black metal.
25. As an artist, I want KHR_materials_unlit honoured, so that a sign or a glow draws at its authored colour.
26. As an artist, I want a JPEG texture skipped with a log, so that I know to export PNG.
27. As a player, I want highlights on the ball, so that it reads as a shiny sphere.
28. As a player, I want metal surfaces to keep their colour in shade, so that they do not go black without an environment map.
29. As a game author, I want light colours in physical units, so that glTF lights and engine lights mean the same thing.
30. As a game author, I want point lights to fall off with inverse square inside their range, so that they match glTF and Filament.
31. As a game author, I want to name a cubemap sky in my Scene, so that the background fits my world.
32. As a game author, I want sky 0 to mean no sky, so that the host clears to black.
33. As an artist, I want the sky drawn at its authored colour, so that the tone map does not darken it.
34. As an artist, I want a sky as six PNGs named px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz, so that common tools export it directly.
35. As a Kula player, I want each level to have its own Theme, so that the three levels look different.
36. As a Kula player, I want finishing a level to start the next after a short pause, so that the game flows.
37. As a Kula player, I want finishing level 3 to end in Won, so that the game has an end.
38. As a Kula player, I want the level change to show no magenta, so that the swap is clean.
39. As a Kula author, I want a Theme record to hold its pack, asset names, lights and sun, so that one table defines a world.
40. As a Kula author, I want textures and skies generated by scripts, so that no original assets enter the repo.
41. As an engine maintainer, I want the pack lifecycle tested through the host-game seam, so that the tests check behaviour, not internals.
42. As an engine maintainer, I want each asset table to reuse freed slots safely, so that streaming never runs out of slots early.

## Implementation Decisions

Packs and the seam:
- Pack is the engine term. CONTEXT.md and docs/GLOSSARY.md gain Pack; Level leaves the engine vocabulary and goes in Pack's Avoid list. ADR 0003 records "Packs own asset lifetimes".
- Command gains Load({ pack : Str, assets : List(Str) }) and Unload(Str).
- init changes to Config -> { model, commands }.
- A fourth seam function: loaded : Model, Str, Manifest -> Model. Manifest is List({ name : Str, id : U32 }).
- Config carries assets : List(Str), the names found on disk, with no ids. Mesh names are file stems from assets/meshes/. Sky names are sky/<dir> from assets/sky/.
- The host runs each Command after the step that returned it and before view. Load is synchronous, and loaded runs in the same frame. loaded is the only promise that ids exist, so a later background loader changes no game.
- A swap is Load(new), then loaded, then Unload(old) from a later step.
- Only the primitives load at startup. They belong to no pack and never unload.
- Packs are independent. Any number load, and each unloads by name in any order.
- An asset named by several loaded packs loads once and keeps one id. Each asset counts the packs that hold it and unloads at zero.
- GPU resources belong to the asset. Vertex and image data are scratch until upload, so a pack keeps only its name and its asset list.
- The mesh table (64 slots) and a new sky table (16 slots, slot 0 means no sky) use the existing slot-and-generation id and a free list.
- A name not on disk, or a file that fails, gets id 0 in the manifest and one log line.
- Load of a loaded pack, Unload of an unknown pack, and a second Load of one pack in one step each log once per pack name and do nothing.
- The level arena and level_unload are renamed for packs or removed. mesh_table_unload_level becomes per-pack unload.

Textures and materials:
- Vertex gains uv. One vertex format and one pipeline. A mesh with no texture binds a 1x1 white image. The primitives get UVs.
- The glTF loader reads TEXCOORD_0, the base colour texture (PNG from the GLB binary chunk via core:image/png), its sampler, metallicFactor, roughnessFactor, the metallic-roughness texture (G roughness, B metallic, linear) and KHR_materials_unlit. JPEG is skipped with a log.
- glTF defaults apply (both factors 1.0), except that a primitive with no material is grey, metallic 0, roughness 1.
- Base colour and sky images upload as SRGB8A8. Mipmaps are built on the CPU with a 2x2 box filter in linear light, only when the minification filter asks.
- baseColorFactor stays in the vertex colour and multiplies the texture.
- fs_params gains a per-mesh material vec4: roughness, metallic, unlit, spare. The host fills it from the mesh. The Draw does not change.
- The fragment shader gains the camera position.

Lighting:
- BRDF: GGX distribution, height-correlated Smith visibility, Schlick Fresnel with F0 = mix(0.04, base, metallic), Lambert diffuse (1 - metallic) * base / pi. alpha = roughness squared; roughness clamps to at least 0.045. Guard the half vector and every denominator, and write pow(1 - x, 5) as multiplies.
- Ambient: ambient * ((1 - metallic) * base + EnvBRDFApprox(F0, roughness, n.v)), after Karis (2014).
- Light colours follow physical units, with the 1/pi in the BRDF. Every game retunes its lights by pi. DESIGN.md states the convention.
- A point light keeps the windowed falloff and gains 1 / max(d^2, 0.01^2).
- The tint multiplies base colour only. Specular takes no tint.
- No exposure knob. Exposure belongs to the look record proposal (yjtqgdd4).
- Check every BRDF constant against the glTF 2.0 spec Appendix B, Filament and Karis before use. The research that chose them was not checked against those sources.

Sky and unlit:
- Scene gains sky : U32, 0 meaning none.
- The host draws a unit cube around the camera, pinned to the far plane (reversed Z), after the opaque pass.
- The sky and unlit meshes skip the lights and the tone map and draw their texture colour through the sRGB encode.

Kula:
- A kula pack, loaded from init, holds the ball and the assets every Theme shares.
- Three Themes, one per level. A Theme record holds its pack name, asset names, lights and sun direction. A table in Kula code maps each level to its Theme.
- Finishing level N sends Load for Theme N+1. On loaded, Kula switches its ids and starts the level; the next step sends Unload for the old pack. Finishing level 3 keeps Won.
- Levels 2 and 3 are hand-written .txt files in the existing format.
- make_meshes.py packs Blender-made PNG textures into each face .glb, sets UVs and metallic 0, and gives the ball a low roughness. A sibling Blender script renders six sky PNGs per Theme. The outputs are committed. No original assets.

Order: (1) Pack term and docs, (2) seam: Commands, loaded, init commands, Config names, glue, port cards, entity-game and Kula, (3) host tables: free lists, refcounts, packs, (4) textures and PBR, (5) sky, (6) Kula content. Steps 1 to 3 change nothing on screen. Steps 4 and 5 each need only step 3.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test drives behaviour through the highest seam and checks what a game or the screen would see, not table internals.
- The pack lifecycle is tested through the host-game seam with the fake game (prior art: seam_test.odin, including the command-before-view test) and a temporary assets directory (prior art: temp_mesh_dir in mesh_load_test.odin). Cover: init Load, loaded before view, a swap with no stale id, a shared asset's refcount, a missing name with id 0, and each nonsense Command logged once.
- glTF reading is tested with GLB bytes built in test code (prior art: gltf_test.odin): UVs, an embedded PNG, the sampler, the material factors, the defaults and the unlit extension.
- Image preparation is tested as plain procedures: PNG decode, sRGB format choice, linear-light mipmap sizes and values.
- Frame render is tested through its capture (prior art: frame_render_test.odin): the per-mesh material values and the sky draw.
- Kula is tested with Roc expect: the Theme table, and the order Load, loaded, then Unload in the next step.
- The shaders are checked by eye: each game runs under ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES and a person looks at the result. The GPU upload is not unit-tested; tests keep zero buffer ids and the destroy guard.
- The full suite runs once at the end of each task: odin test engine, host-check.sh, each game's roc test and the build script tests.

## Out of Scope

- Pong. ntbh6adj brings it back in line and includes the pack seam.
- Background loading. The seam allows it; the host loads synchronously.
- Runtime-generated assets sent from Roc.
- Image-based lighting, sky reflections, hemisphere ambient, normal maps, emissive and occlusion.
- An exposure knob and a choice of tone map (yjtqgdd4).
- Shadows (Milestone 13), the HUD (Milestone 14), fog (s1zhf2hf) and the pickup flash (nafp0q3s).
- Raising MESH_CAPACITY.

## Further Notes

- Part of 'The second arc' (docs/ROADMAP.md). Blocked by Milestone 11, which is done.
- jzvojfn9 (mesh id generation) is done. Its mesh_table_unload_level is the start of step 3.
- The Kula SPEC.md Theme definition ("a sky, a set of lights and a set of block meshes") maps directly to a pack plus a lights record.
result: Packs load and unload through Load, loaded and Unload with refcounted shared assets and generation ids. Meshes draw glTF base colour textures and metallic-roughness materials under a GGX BRDF. Scene.sky draws a cubemap. Kula plays three levels, each in its own Theme pack with a textured face and a Blender-rendered sky. User checked all three levels by eye on 2026-10-15: no magenta.

name: The loader reads one Skin and its Clips
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Read one Skin and its Clips from a .glb, and publish the Clips in the
Manifest. See the milestone task for the decisions. No sampling and no GPU
skinning are in this task.

## What to build

- In `engine/gltf.odin`, read `skins`, `JOINTS_0`, `WEIGHTS_0`,
  `inverseBindMatrices` and `animations` (samplers and channels with
  translation, rotation and scale). Widen `glb_accessor` for the needed
  component types and VEC4/MAT4.
- A .glb with a Skin loads as one skinned mesh in bind-pose space: do not
  bake world space for it. Files with no Skin load exactly as today.
- Load errors, each with a clear message: more than one Skin, mixed skinned
  and unskinned mesh nodes, more than 64 Joints, CUBICSPLINE keys.
- Add `Skinned_Vertex` (56 bytes, joints and normalised weights as u8x4)
  and keep the Skin (Joint parents, inverse bind matrices, rest TRS) and
  the Clips (keys per Joint channel, duration) in the mesh table.
- Pad the box of a skinned mesh by 25% of its largest extent.
- Assign Clip ids, unique across the Pack, from 1, and fill each Manifest
  entry's `clips` with name, id and duration.
- Pure Odin tests on the fixture from the rig task: Joint count, Clip
  names, durations, key counts, weights that sum to 1, the padded box, and
  each load error (build the bad inputs in the test).

## Done when

- `odin test engine` covers the above on every runner.
- Chapter 10's future `pip.glb` loads as a skinned mesh, and chapters 1 to
  9 still draw (a skinned mesh draws in its bind pose until the GPU task;
  draw it through the rigid path with the joints ignored if that is the
  smallest step).
- The Manifest of a pack with `pip` lists Idle and Walk.
result: The loader reads one Skin and its Clips. New engine/skin.odin holds the storage (Skin, Joint, Joint_Trs, Clip, Clip_Channel, Influence, Skinned_Vertex, MAX_JOINTS, mesh_clip, clip_channels, channel_keys). New engine/gltf_skin.odin reads the Skin and Clips. Joints are stored parent first; each Joint's base holds the non-Joint nodes above it (Blender's armature). Mesh keeps skin and first_clip; Mesh_Table.next_clip gives Clip ids from 1, never reused. A skinned box is padded by 25% of its largest side. seam_load fills each Manifest entry's clips. Errors: Two_Skins, Mixed_Skinning, Too_Many_Joints, Cubic_Spline, No_Influences, Bad_Skin, Bad_Clip; note Channel_Skipped. Skinned meshes still upload as 48-byte Vertex and draw in bind pose. Tests: 474 pass in both builds; test-all, run-games chapters 1-9 and alloc check pass.

commit.message: feat(animation): Load one Skin and its Clips from a .glb

description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Tracer bullet with no Vocabulary change. See the milestone nmpfj41t and ADR 0011.

## What to build

  that the tag ships stb_vorbis (for example `extras/stb_vorbis.c`). If it
  does not, stop and report.

- Copy the archive into `platform/targets/<target>/` from
  `roc scripts/build.roc inputs`. Name it in `platform/main.roc` for each
  target.
- Write thin Odin bindings in `engine/` for the `ma_engine` calls this task
  needs: init, uninit, and the config with `noDevice`.
- Add `dlopen` and the thread symbols miniaudio calls to the macOS sysroot
  catalog, the Linux stubs and the Windows import libraries, with evidence.
  Run each `--audit`.
- At startup, the host creates an `ma_engine`. Headless creates it with no
  device. If the device does not open, the host logs once and continues
  silent. The host uninits it at shutdown.

## Done when

- Every example game builds and runs in CI on macOS, Linux (xvfb, no audio
  device) and Windows.
- A Linux run with no audio device logs one line and exits 0.
- A Headless run opens no device.
result: miniaudio 0.11.24 is a submodule, and each target builds one archive with stb_vorbis. The inputs step copies the archive and platform/main.roc names it. engine/miniaudio.odin binds ma_engine init, uninit and its config. name: Milestone 17: Launch
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

A game cannot decide anything before its window opens. The window size,
`high_dpi`, the MSAA sample count, vsync, the fixed step rate, the shadow map
size and the table capacities are host constants. Every game gets 960 by 540,
no `high_dpi`, 4x MSAA, 120 Hz, a 2048 shadow map, 64 meshes, 16 skies and
16,384 Draws. Nothing goes from the game to the host at start-up. Config goes
the other way.

The costs today:

- A Retina Mac renders every game at half resolution and scales it up (dex
  me0izszb).
- A game cannot trade shadow sharpness for GPU cost. The Kula shadow edge is
  soft and the only fix is a host constant (dex z851lo4y).
- A bench game that needs 16,384 Draws depends on a constant that pong also
  pays for: a 12.6 MB uniform buffer and a pairing map reserved for 4,096.
- A 2D game, a 60 Hz game or a fullscreen game cannot exist without an engine
  edit.

## Solution

A fifth required call, `launch : Config -> Launch`. The host calls it once,
before `init` and before the window opens, with the same Config that `init`
gets. A Launch is what the game decides once: its window, its step rate, its
shadow map size and its capacities. `pf.Launch.default` is today's constants
with one change, `high_dpi` on, so a game that wants the defaults writes
`launch = |_config| Launch.default`.

The game reads its Args in `launch`, so `--fullscreen` or `--size 1280x720` is
the game's decision, as ADR 0006 intends. ADR 0007 records the decision, the
three rejected homes and the rules that bind later work. CONTEXT.md holds the
terms `launch` and `Launch` under "The five calls" and "The vocabulary".

## User Stories

1. As a game author, I want to define `launch`, so that my game decides its
   window before the window opens.
2. As a game author, I want `launch = |_config| Launch.default` to be enough,
   so that the fifth call costs one line.
3. As a game author, I want `launch` to receive the same Config as `init`, so
   that a `--fullscreen` or `--size` Arg is my game's decision.
4. As a game author, I want a width and a height in Launch, so that my game
   opens at the size it was designed for.
5. As a game author, I want a title in Launch, so that the window names my
   game instead of the engine.
6. As a game author, I want `fullscreen` in Launch, so that a game that starts
   fullscreen does not open windowed and then jump.
7. As a game author, I want `high_dpi` in Launch, so that my game renders at
   the display's full resolution on a Retina Mac.
8. As a game author, I want `samples` as the tag `Msaa`, so that I cannot ask
   for three samples.
9. As a game author, I want `vsync` in Launch, so that my game chooses between
   tearing and latency.
10. As a game author, I want `step_hz` in Launch, so that my game chooses its
    fixed step rate and `step` sees the matching `dt`.
11. As a game author, I want `shadow_map` in Launch, so that I can trade shadow
    sharpness for GPU cost.
12. As a game author, I want capacities for meshes, skies, draws and UI quads,
    so that a big game can grow and a small game stays small.
13. As a game author, I want the host to exit with the field's name on a bad
    Launch, so that a typo cannot change my run silently.
14. As a game author, I want `launch` to be pure and total, so that `roc test`
    checks it from `Config.empty` with no fixture.
15. As a game author, I want hot reload to keep my window, so that a start-up
    setting stays a start-up setting until I restart.
16. As a game author, I want the docs on each Launch field to say whether a
    Scene field may replace it later, so that I know what can change at run
    time.
17. As a game author, I want `Launch`, `Window`, `Msaa` and `Capacity` in
    `pf.Vocabulary`, so that I import them the way I import Config.
18. As a game author, I want `pf.Launch.default`, so that Launch follows
    `pf.Draw.default` and `pf.Scene.empty`.
19. As a game author, I want a Launch past a capacity at run time to keep
    today's rule, so that a Scene with too many Draws logs once and draws the
    first N.
20. As a bench game, I want `high_dpi` off, so that my numbers do not depend
    on the display.
21. As a bench game, I want to size `draws` from my N Arg, so that the pairing
    map and the uniform buffer match the workload.
22. As an Odin twin, I want to supply a `launch` through Game calls, so that
    a twin build runs the same start-up as its bench game.
23. As the engine author, I want the default Launch to equal today's
    constants except `high_dpi`, so that no existing game changes behaviour on
    the day Launch lands, except for a sharper picture.
24. As the engine author, I want the four fixed arrays to become allocations
    sized at `launch`, so that the capacity constants leave the engine.
25. As the engine author, I want the pairing map sized from `draws`, so that
    the step in the Draws curve above 4,096 moves with the capacity.
26. As the engine author, I want the uniform buffer, the texture pool and the
    shadow map image sized from Launch, so that the GPU resources match the
    tables.
27. As the engine author, I want the Seam to call `launch` before `init`, so
    that the order lives in one place and the fake game proves it.
28. As the engine author, I want Game calls to carry `launch`, so that the
    fake game and the Odin twins supply one.
29. As the engine author, I want the glue regenerated from the new header, so
    that `roc_launch` and the Launch types come from `roc glue` and never by
    hand.
30. As the engine author, I want the window options to come from one pure
    function of a Launch and a run mode, so that they are tested without
    sokol.
31. As the engine author, I want the Launch check to be a pure function that
    names the bad field, so that the exit path is tested without exiting.
32. As the engine author, I want the clock to take `step_hz` at init, so that
    the fixed interval constant leaves the engine.
33. As the engine author, I want `ui_quads` capped at 16,384, so that the u16
    index buffer cannot overflow.
34. As the engine author, I want a frame-cost measurement with `high_dpi` on
    and off, so that me0izszb closes with a number.
35. As the engine author, I want a screenshot on a Retina Mac at the doubled
    size, so that I can see the change and check that the HUD keeps its
    logical size.
36. As the engine author, I want z851lo4y completed with a pointer to the look
    half, so that yjtqgdd4 and s1zhf2hf carry the shader knobs.
37. As the person who runs a game, I want Lockstep to turn vsync off whatever
    Launch says, so that frame pacing does not hide CPU time.
38. As the person who runs a game, I want Headless to lay out the UI against
    Launch's width and height at dpi 1, so that a Headless run's UI matches
    the game's window.
39. As the person who runs a game, I want every `ROCCO_*` variable to keep its
    meaning, so that my choices about one run stay mine.
40. As a CI maintainer, I want the host check to fail when the glue drifts
    from the header, so that a Launch field change cannot ship a stale host.
41. As a CI maintainer, I want every example, bench game and package to pass
    `roc check` and `roc test` with the fifth call, so that test-all stays
    green.
42. As the Kula author, I want the change recorded as a Vocabulary change, so
    that Kula adds `launch` when it moves to the next bundle.
43. As a reader of the docs, I want DESIGN.md, the README and the glossary to
    say five calls, so that the docs match the header.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Glossary.** The spec uses `launch`, Launch, Config, Args, Seed,
  Vocabulary, Vocabulary change, Seam, Game calls, Glue, Fixed step, dt,
  Frame, Lockstep, Headless, Bench game, Odin twin, Pack, Mesh table,
  Fallback mesh, Primitive and UI from CONTEXT.md. ADR 0006 and ADR 0007
  bind the design.
- **The header.** The platform's `requires` gains `launch : Config ->
  Launch`. `provides` gains `roc_launch`, listed before `roc_init` because it
  runs first. `exposes` gains the Launch module. The host wrapper passes the
  record through with no box, because a Launch has no Model.
- **The types.** Launch has four fields: `window`, `step_hz`, `shadow_map`
  and `capacity`. Window has seven: `width`, `height`, `title`, `fullscreen`,
  `high_dpi`, `samples` and `vsync`. `samples` is the tag `Msaa` with `Off`,
  `X2`, `X4` and `X8`. Capacity has four: `meshes`, `skies`, `draws` and
  `ui_quads`. All counts are `U32`. ADR 0007 holds the exact shape. Launch,
  Window, Msaa and Capacity join the Vocabulary.
- **The defaults.** `pf.Launch.default` is 960 by 540, title "rocco",
  windowed, `high_dpi` on, `X4`, vsync on, 120 Hz, a 2048 shadow map, and 64
  meshes, 16 skies, 16,384 draws and 16,384 UI quads.
- **The Launch module.** A platform module in the pattern of the Draw and
  Scene modules: it exposes `default` and an `expect` that pins it.
- **Game calls.** The struct gains `launch`. The Roc game, the fake game and
  both Odin twins supply one. The Odin twins return the default with
  `high_dpi` off, as their bench games do.
- **The Seam.** The Seam calls `launch` before `init`. The host calls the
  Seam for the Launch first, sizes its tables from it, then calls the Seam's
  init, which runs init's Commands. The order is one visible sequence in the
  host's start-up, and the fake game observes it.
- **Host start-up order.** Read the environment. Call `launch`. Check the
  Launch. Size the mesh table, the sky table, the Pack reference arrays, the
  frame render tables, the pairing map and the UI quads from the capacities.
  Init the clock from `step_hz`. Call `init` through the Seam. Then either
  run Headless or open the window with the options from the Launch.
- **The Launch check.** A pure function returns the name of the first bad
  field, or none. Bad means: a zero in any numeric field, `ui_quads` past
  16,384, `meshes` below four (the Fallback mesh and the three Primitives),
  and `skies` below two (the reserved slot and one sky). The host prints the
  field with the rule it broke and exits with status 1, as a bad
  `ROCCO_SEED` does. The two minimums refine the grilling's "a zero in any
  numeric field": a table that cannot hold what the engine puts in it at
  start-up is the same fault.
- **The window options.** One pure function takes a Launch and a run mode and
  returns the sokol description: width, height, title, the sample count from
  the Msaa tag with `Off` as one, `high_dpi`, `fullscreen`, and vsync.
  Lockstep turns vsync off whatever the Launch says. This replaces today's
  function of the run mode alone.
- **The clock.** The clock takes `step_hz` at init and keeps the fixed
  interval as a field. `dt` to `step` is one over `step_hz`. Lockstep adds
  one interval per Frame. The maximum Frame time stays a host constant.
- **The renderer.** The pipelines take the sample count from the Launch. The
  shadow map image takes `shadow_map` for both sides. The uniform buffer
  size follows `draws`. The texture pool follows `meshes` and `skies`.
- **The tables.** The mesh table, the sky table and the Pack reference arrays
  become slices allocated once from the permanent allocator at the Launch's
  capacity. The frame render's placed list and pairing map reserve `draws`.
  The UI quads take `ui_quads`, which the UI init already accepts. The UI
  element count stays a Clay constant. Past a capacity at run time the host
  keeps today's rule: log once, draw the first N.
- **Headless.** The Headless platform record is built from the Launch: its
  UI window is the Launch's width and height at dpi 1. It ignores title,
  samples, vsync, fullscreen and `high_dpi`.
- **The glue.** The glue names each record by the first path that reaches
  it from a `provides` entry, and later paths become aliases. With
  `roc_launch` first, Config takes its name from the launch argument and the
  init argument becomes an alias. The host's alias lines change to match,
  and gain Launch, Window, Msaa and Capacity. The generated file is
  regenerated through the build script and never edited.
- **The games.** The three examples add `launch` to their app list and define
  it as the default. The seven bench games define it as the default with
  `high_dpi` off. The Draws and Mixed bench games also set `draws` from the
  N Arg through the shared bench helpers, and fall back to the default when
  N is missing, because `init` already stops the run on a bad N.
- **The docs.** DESIGN.md section 2 becomes the five functions and its
  entrypoint list gains `roc_launch`. The README's hot reload section says a
  changed `launch` needs a restart. The README's game-writing section shows
  the fifth call. CONTEXT.md and ADR 0007 are already written in the
  worktree.
- **dex.** me0izszb completes with the measurement in its result. z851lo4y
  completes with a result that says the start-up half landed in Milestone 17
  and the look half lives in yjtqgdd4 and s1zhf2hf.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test checks what a caller sees: the Seam's calls on the game, a pure
  function's result, or a table's behaviour at its edge. It does not check
  internal steps. The one ordering fact, `launch` before `init`, is a
  promise to the game, so the fake game observes it as the game would.
- **The Seam.** The fake game gains `launch`. It records the call count and
  the Config it saw. Tests check that the host calls `launch` once, before
  `init`, with a Config equal to the one `init` gets: the same Seed, asset
  names and Args. Prior art: the Seam tests that check the Seed, the asset
  names and the Args reach `init`.
- **The Launch check.** Table tests over bad Launches: each zero field, the
  UI quads bound, the mesh and sky minimums, and the default passing. Prior
  art: the Seed and run-mode rejection tests.
- **The window options.** Tests build the description from a Launch and each
  run mode and check every field, the Msaa mapping, and vsync off only in
  Lockstep. Prior art: the existing test that vsync turns off only in
  Lockstep.
- **The clock and the Frame.** Frame tests at a non-default `step_hz`, such
  as 60, check one step per interval in real-clock mode and one step per
  Frame in Lockstep. Prior art: the frame tests at the fixed dt.
- **Headless.** A test checks the Headless UI window equals the Launch's
  width and height at dpi 1. Prior art: the Headless frame tests.
- **The tables.** The mesh table, sky table and frame render tests construct
  their tables at a small capacity and check the full-table result and the
  log-once-and-drop rule at that capacity. Prior art: the existing mesh,
  sky, pack and frame render tests at the constants.
- **The Roc side.** The Launch module pins `default` with an `expect`. Each
  example expects `launch(Config.empty)` equal to the default. Each bench
  game expects `high_dpi` off. `roc test` runs them through test-all.
- **The glue.** The tracer bullet regenerates the glue and the host builds
  against it. The host check already fails when the generated file drifts
  from the header. No new glue test.
- **Not tested by code.** The window opening at the size, the exit message
  text, and the `high_dpi` frame cost. The first two are a manual check with
  the screenshot script. The third is a measurement with the bench harness
  in windowed Lockstep, recorded in me0izszb's result.

## Out of Scope

- `Scene.window`: fullscreen and title at run time, and the cursor rule
  change. ADR 0007 records the rule for that step.
- The Look record: tone map, exposure, fog, the shadow biases, the normal
  offset and the PCF kernel or PCSS. dex yjtqgdd4 and s1zhf2hf.
- `extensions` in Launch. It waits for the extension ABI.
- A failure path for `launch`, or a `Quit` that carries a reason.
- Icon, clipboard and drag-and-drop options.
- The cascade count. It stays an engine constant; dex 75ah1rr3.
- The game learning the window size or aspect ratio; dex elqpa9x2.
- Growing a table at run time past its capacity.
- The UI element count as a capacity.
- A ROADMAP.md section. Milestones since 16 live in dex.
- Kula's own change. It lives in Pixelsprout/kula.
- A visual check on Linux or Windows. CI runs Headless there.

## Further Notes

- **Order of work.** Tracer bullet first: the header, the regenerated glue,
  `launch` in Game calls, the fake game test, and the default Launch feeding
  today's constants unchanged. Then the window options and `high_dpi`, the
  step rate, the capacities, the renderer sizes, the games, the docs, the
  measurement and the dex closures.
- **The Draws curve.** The benchmarks method document reports a step above
  4,096 Draws from the pairing map reservation. Once the Draws bench game
  sizes `draws` from N, that step moves or goes. The method document gets a
  note when the next reference run is taken, not in this milestone.
- **Hot reload.** `launch` runs once per process. Under `roc run`, a changed
  `launch` takes effect on restart. The README says so.
- **Arg parsing.** The platform gives no parser for `--size WxH`. A game
  parses its own Args, as ADR 0006 decided. A shared package can come later
  if three games want the same flags.
- **The worktree.** CONTEXT.md and ADR 0007 are edited and uncommitted in the
  `m17-launch` worktree. They commit with this spec's dex entry before the
  first ticket starts.
result: A fifth call, launch : Config -> Launch, sets the window, step rate, shadow map size and capacities before the window opens; merged to main in b11e71b.

name: Milestone 20: Audio
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

The engine plays no sound. `guide/install.md` says "No audio yet". Kula has
no landing sound (x7mwcd0w), and the arc check needs one.

## Solution

miniaudio in the host. A game returns what should be heard as data: a
`Play` Command for a sound that plays once, and a Loop in `Scene.loops`
for a sound that repeats. Sounds are Pack assets with ids in the Manifest.

Done when Kula plays a landing sound on macOS, Linux and Windows, from the
v0.3.0 release URLs.

Check:
- The Bridge `step` reply shows a `Play` when Kula's ball lands.
- A host test mixes a Play with no device and finds samples that are not
  zero.
- A person hears the bounce on each target.

## Decisions (grilled 2026-10-22)

- Backend: miniaudio 0.11.24 as a submodule, with stb_vorbis. Our own build
  scripts make one archive per target, in the same way as sokol. Windows
  uses `/Zl /GS-`. The engine has thin Odin bindings of its own and does
  not import `vendor:miniaudio`. ADR 0011 records this, and why not saudio
  or FMOD.
- Linking: miniaudio opens the audio libraries at run time. The catalogs
  gain `dlopen` and the thread symbols (pthread on macOS and Linux;
  `CreateThread`, the events and the waits on Windows), with evidence. No
  audio library joins a catalog. `MA_NO_RUNTIME_LINKING` waits for
  notarization.
- Device: the host always creates an `ma_engine`. Headless creates it with
  no device. If the device does not open, the host logs once and the run
  is silent. While the Bridge pauses Lockstep, sound plays on.
- Vocabulary (one change):
  - `Play({ sound : U32, gain : F32, pitch : F32, at : Place })`.
  - `Scene.loops : List(Loop)`, with
    `Loop : { id : U64, sound : U32, gain : F32, pitch : F32, at : Place }`.
  - `Place : [Here, At({ pos : Vec3, range : F32 })]`.
  - `Capacity` gains `sounds` (default 64) and `voices` (default 64).
  - `pf.Sound.play(id)` returns a Play with gain 1, pitch 1, `Here`.
    `pf.Loop.default` follows `pf.Draw.default`.
- Values: gain is linear; 1 is as recorded; a negative gain plays as 0.
  Pitch is a rate; 1 is as recorded; 0 or less logs once and plays at 1.
- Place: the Listener is the Camera of the current Scene, set once per
  fixed step, not interpolated. `At` falls off linearly to zero at
  `range`, as a Point Light does. `Here` plays at the Listener with no
  direction.
- Loops: a new Loop id starts, a missing id stops with a short host fade, a
  changed gain, pitch or place applies on the next fixed step, and a
  changed Sound id restarts. No repeat flag. Music that plays once is a
  Play.
- Voices: when full, a Play takes the voice of the oldest Play, and a new
  Loop waits silent for a free voice. Each case logs once.
- Bad ids: Sound id 0 or a stale id plays nothing and logs once. No
  fallback sound.
- Unload: the host stops the voices of a Sound before it frees the Sound.
- Assets: `.wav` and `.ogg` in `assets/sound/`, named `sound/<stem>`, chosen
  by the prefix. A shared stem loads the first file in sorted order and
  logs once. The host decodes each Sound fully at load. `Config.assets`
  lists meshes, then skies, then Sounds.
- No master volume and no audio pause. A game scales its own gains. A
  package can add helpers later.
- Terms: Sound, Sound id, Play, Loop, Loop id, Listener and Voice are in
  CONTEXT.md. ADR 0012 records the Play and Loop split, which replaces the
  Spawn and Destroy plan in DESIGN.md section 6.
- Tutorial chapter 8, "Sound": a blip on a pickup (Play), a hum at the door
  (placed Loop) and a background Loop. `make_sounds.py` synthesizes the
  wav files, so no licence applies.
- Kula: a synthesized bounce in Kula's `assets/sound/`. Kula moves its
  header to v0.3.0, which this milestone cuts.

## Out of scope

- Streaming from disk.
- flac and mp3.
- A master volume, a mute or an audio pause.
- Stopping a Play.
- FMOD, which waits for the extension arc.
- Notarization on macOS.

## Tasks in order

See the subtasks. The first two can run in parallel.

1. njvgfhx5: miniaudio in the host (tracer bullet, any time).
2. ulp6x0tr: The audio Vocabulary change (any time, parallel with 1).
3. c3xeld0l: Sounds as Pack assets (after 1 and 2).
4. iwtl4wj2: Play: voices, the Listener and the mixer test (after 3).
5. ynjedxit: Loops: pair Scene.loops by Loop id (after 4).
6. m1bilkmv: Tutorial chapter 8 and the sound guide (after 5).
7. ifrcq18g: Cut v0.3.0 (after 6).
8. x7mwcd0w: Kula: landing sound, in the Kula repo (after 7).

When the milestone closes, complete 79n12xde ("Audio via saudio"): ADR 0011
chose miniaudio in its place.
result: Milestone 20: Audio is done. miniaudio 0.11.24 runs in the host (PR #5, merged as 59e0b3c). A game plays a Sound with a Play Command and keeps a Loop in Scene.loops. Sounds are Pack assets. v0.3.0 is published, pixelsprout.dev shows guide/sound.md and tutorial chapter 8, and Kula plays a landing bounce from v0.3.0 (kula PR #1). A host test mixes a Play with no device and finds samples that are not zero. CI passes on macOS, Linux and Windows. The user heard Plays on macOS.

name: A default for every record a game builds
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

## Parent

Beside the milestones (6xjrehjc). Source: docs/RESEARCH-SCALING.md, section 6,
"A default for every record a game builds", and "A proposed order", item 1.

## Why

A game writes Scene and Draw as record literals. Every field added to a
Vocabulary record breaks every game and every game test. Launch, Look, Ports
and Audio each add fields. A default per record, used with record update,
makes each later Vocabulary addition cost old games nothing. Ui.default_box
and QueryResults.empty are the precedents. This is not a Vocabulary change.

## What to build

Add four platform modules beside pf.Light and pf.Collider. Each one holds one
value and its expects.

1. pf.Scene: `empty : Vocabulary.Scene`. No draws, colliders, lights, ui or
   queries. Cursor Free. Sky 0. A valid camera: eye at { 0, 5, 10 }, target
   at the origin, up along y, fov_y 1.047 (the camera package's default).
2. pf.Draw: `default : Vocabulary.Draw`. Id 0, mesh 0 (the fallback mesh),
   pos zero, scale one, rot and scale_rot the identity quaternion, tint white.
3. pf.Config: `empty : Vocabulary.Config`. Seed 0, no assets. On main, Config
   has no Args yet; the m16-benchmarks branch adds `args`. When that branch
   lands, add `args: []` here and nowhere else.
4. pf.Input: `empty : Vocabulary.Input`. Nothing held, nothing pressed,
   mouse delta zero.

Add each module to `exposes` and to the matching imports in platform/main.roc.
Update the exposes list in docs/DESIGN.md and the platform file table in
README.md. In CONTEXT.md, name the default in the Scene, Draw, Config and
Input entries, as the Light entry names pf.Light. Do not add glossary terms.

Then port the three example games (examples/cards, examples/entity-game,
examples/pong):

- Every Scene literal in `view` becomes `{ ..Scene.empty, ... }` and sets
  only the fields the game decides.
- Every Draw literal, including the `box` and `draw` helpers, becomes
  `{ ..Draw.default, ... }`.
- Every Config literal in a test becomes `Config.empty` or
  `{ ..Config.empty, assets: [...] }`. Replace pong's `no_assets`.

name: Linux: evdev and inotify
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

The Linux backend of Milestone 23. See the milestone task.

## What to build

- Add `engine/gamepad_linux.odin`. Use `core:sys/linux` syscalls only, so
  the Linux stubs get no new symbol.
- At startup, scan `/dev/input/event*`. Open each node read-only and
  non-blocking. Keep a node whose `EVIOCGBIT` key bits include
  `BTN_GAMEPAD`. Read the `ABS` ranges with `EVIOCGABS`.
- Watch `/dev/input` with `inotify`. When a new `event` node appears, try
  to open it. If the open fails with `EACCES`, try again on the next
  frames for about 1 s. When a read fails with `ENODEV`, the pad is gone.
- Each frame, read the pending events of each pad without blocking.
- Write a pure procedure from a list of evdev events and the `ABS` ranges
  to the host Gamepad state. Map the kernel gamepad layout: `BTN_SOUTH`
  and the others, `ABS_X`/`ABS_Y`, `ABS_RX`/`ABS_RY`, `ABS_Z`/`ABS_RZ` for
  the triggers, and `ABS_HAT0X`/`ABS_HAT0Y` for the D-pad. The Odin tests
  drive it on every runner.

## Done when

- The mapping tests pass on every runner, with event lists from `xpad`.
- With no pad, the Linux CI run (xvfb) reports an empty list and does not
  crash.
- `scripts/make_linux_stubs.py --audit` shows no new symbol in the Linux stubs.

The manual check on Linux is a separate task.

## Decided after research (2026-10-26)

See `notes/os-backends.md` section 3 in the scratchpad notes folder.
- X and Y: `xpad` reports the Xbox X button (West) as 0x133, the code of
  `BTN_NORTH`, and Y (North) as 0x134, `BTN_WEST`. When a pad connects,
  read its driver name with `readlink` on
  `/sys/class/input/eventN/device/device/driver`. Swap 0x133 and 0x134 for
  `xpad` only. Every other driver follows `gamepad.rst`. The mapping
  procedure takes the swap as an input, and the tests cover both cases.
- The symbol check is `scripts/make_linux_stubs.py --audit`, not
  `host-check.sh`.
- The CI container may have no `/dev/input`. A missing folder means no
  pads, with no error.
- Put the pure mapping procedure in a file with no OS suffix.
result: The Linux reader (engine/gamepad_linux.odin) scans /dev/input at startup, watches it with inotify, retries EACCES for about 1 s and reads evdev through core:sys/linux. engine/gamepad_evdev.odin maps the events with no OS calls, swaps 0x133 and 0x134 for xpad (driver name from sysfs) and latches key-down events so a sub-frame tap survives (a22990f). Odin tests pass on macOS and in the rocco-linux container; the stub audit finds no new symbol. uinput virtual pads confirmed scan, hot-plug and removal. The real xpad check is xsl5lr4n.

commit.message: feat(engine): Add the Linux gamepad backend on evdev and inotify

name: Seam and host: run commands from step, cursor from Scene
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

Change the seam so step returns commands and the host runs them. See the decisions in Milestone 9 (fbyluoga).

## Requirements

1. In platform/Vocabulary.roc, add Command : [Quit] and Cursor : [Free, Locked].
2. Add cursor : Cursor to Scene.
3. In platform/main.roc, change the step requirement to return { model : Model, commands : List(Vocabulary.Command) }.
4. Change step_for_host to return { model : Box(Model), commands : List(Command) }.
5. Regenerate the glue with roc scripts/build.roc -- glue.
6. In engine/seam.odin, keep the returned model pointer. Run each command in list order after step and before view.
7. For Quit, call sapp.request_quit(). Let the current frame finish.
8. Decref the commands list after the host runs it. Do not keep it in Seam.

11. Remove the ESC branch and its comment from event_cb. The game still sees the key.
12. Add Odin tests in engine/seam_test.odin for command order and list release, where the test setup allows.

## Not in scope

- No hosted block and no => signature in platform/main.roc.
- No replay recorder.
- No new Command tags.

## Done when

- The host builds and the host check passes.
- No hosted function exists in the platform header.
- The tracking allocator reports no leak after a run that emits Quit.

Quit calls sapp.request_quit. frame_cb sets the mouse lock from Scene.cursor, or Locked with the debug camera. ESC left event_cb. Games got the minimum to link: update, a thin step with commands: [], cursor: Free. The order test can only check count and timing, because Command has no tag byte. Real Roc does not heap-allocate a [Quit, Quit] list; a run that emitted it showed no leak.
