name: Engine: scale a Draw along a world axis
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: grilling

## Question

How does a Draw squash a spinning mesh along a world axis? Kula needs this for the idle bob (ekx01utd) and for the jump stretch (42fsutrf).

## What exists

- The host builds the model matrix as T * R * S (engine/transform.odin). Draw.scale acts in model space, before rot.
- The Kula ball's rot is its spin. A model-space scale therefore squashes along an axis that spins with the ball.
- The original builds Orient * Morph * Spin (kula-world-decomp player_movement.c:1025-1027). The morph acts in the ball's frame, after the spin.
- T * R * S cannot express Orient * Morph * Spin for a non-uniform Morph.
- basic.glsl transforms normals by the model matrix, not by its inverse transpose. For the bob's scale (1.05, 1.05, 0.9) a 45 degree normal is off by about 9 degrees.

## Options

1. Add a scale frame to Draw: model = T * R * F * S * F^-1. F is a Quat. It defaults to identity.
2. Add a world-space squash to Draw, an axis and an amount, applied after R.
3. Let Draw carry a full 3x3 linear part in place of rot and scale. This loses the slerp of rot between Scenes.

Each option changes the vocabulary, the glue and the Draw interpolation. docs/DESIGN.md section 3 governs.

## Done when

- DESIGN.md records the choice.
- The shader uses the inverse transpose for normals, or the docs say why not.
result: Option 1: Draw.scale_rot. Model = T*R*F*S*F^-1; the host slerps F. The shader uses normal_model, the inverse transpose. DESIGN.md 'A scale acts along its own axes' and ADR 0002 record it.

commit.message: feat(engine): Scale a Draw along scale_rot and copy the Kula idle bob - Draw gains scale_rot. The model is T * R * F * S * F^-1, and the host slerps F between Scenes. - The shader lights normals with the inverse transpose. engine/transform.odin is gone. - linalg adds Quat.conjugate and Quat.between. Every game sends Quat.identity for scale_rot. - Kula squashes the ball along up at the full-clock rate, 2.05 s a bob, and keeps it on the floor. - DESIGN.md, CONTEXT.md, SPEC.md and ADR 0002 record the scale frame and the bob.

name: Roc view Span varies between processes in the ui bench game
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: research

In the reference run (bench/results/2026-10-21-intel-r-core-tm-i7-9700f-cpu-3-00ghz), the ui bench game has a spread of 16 to 21% of the median at N=128, 512, 1,024 and 16,384. Every other game stays under about 7%, except colliders at N=128 (14%).

The cause is one or two of the 5 processes in which the Roc view Span runs 30 to 40% slower. At N=512, view is 188 us in two processes and 141 us in three. ui_layout is the same in every process, so the effect is in the Roc code or the Roc heap, not in Clay.

Questions: is it memory layout (the Roc heap blocks the view allocates, 2N+4 allocs per step), the core the process runs on, or something else? Does it repeat on the Mac?

Done when: the cause is known, and either fixed or noted in BENCHMARKS.md beside the spread.

name: Milestone 23: Gamepad
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

`Input` carries the keyboard and the mouse delta only. sokol_app reads no
gamepad, and sokol has no gamepad module. Kula and the tutorial cannot be
played with a pad, and the arc check needs Kula on a gamepad.

## Solution

A host module with one file per OS polls the pads beside sokol. `Input`
gains `gamepads : List(Gamepad)`. The Bridge injects pad Input, so CI tests
it with no pad. Tutorial chapter 9 adds the gamepad. The milestone ends
with v0.5.0, and Kula moves to it.

Done when Kula plays with an Xbox pad on macOS and Windows from the v0.5.0
release URLs, and CI tests the mapping procedure of each OS. A person
checks Linux later, in a separate task.

Check:
- `scripts/bridge_check.py` holds South through the Bridge and reads the
  result from the `scene` reply.
- Odin tests drive the mapping procedure of each OS on every runner.
- A person plays Kula with an Xbox pad on macOS and on Windows.
- The alloc check shows no change in the counts with no pad connected.

## Decisions (grilled 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-26)

- Vocabulary (one change):
  - `Input.gamepads : List(Gamepad)`, one entry for each connected pad.
  - `Gamepad : { slot : U8, held : List(U8), pressed : List(U8),
    left_stick : { x : F32, y : F32 }, right_stick : { x : F32, y : F32 },
    left_trigger : F32, right_trigger : F32 }`.
  - The name is `Gamepad`, not `Pad`, because `Pad` can mean padding.
- Buttons: 14 buttons with position names. `South`, `East`, `West`,
  `North`, `LeftShoulder`, `RightShoulder`, `LeftStick`, `RightStick`,
  `Start`, `Back`, `DpadUp`, `DpadDown`, `DpadLeft`, `DpadRight`. No Guide
  button. The triggers are analog only. sokol has no names to follow. The
  position names match the Linux kernel layout and do not depend on the
  pad brand.
- `pf.Button` follows `pf.Key`: the tag union, `Button.code`,
  `Button.held(gamepad, b)`, `Button.pressed(gamepad, b)`,
  `Button.held_any(input, b)` and `Button.pressed_any(input, b)`.
- Values: the host applies one radial dead zone to each stick and rescales
  it to the unit disc. +y is up on every OS. The triggers get a small dead
  zone and go from 0.0 to 1.0. The dead zones are host constants.
- Slots: a pad keeps its slot while it stays connected. A new pad takes the
  lowest free slot. A disconnect removes the entry. The host reports at
  most 4 pads; this is a host constant, not a `Capacity` field. A button
  that is down when its pad connects is held, not pressed.
- Sampling: the host polls each pad once per frame, before the steps of
  that frame. `pressed` collects every button that went down since the
  last step, and a frame with no step keeps them. The axes carry the last
  polled value. On `UNFOCUSED`, the host clears the held buttons and sets
  the axes to zero. XInput polls only, so a tap shorter than one frame can
  be lost. We accept this.
- Backends. Each adds zero catalog entries:
  - macOS: `GameController.framework`, opened with `dlopen`, and our own
    thin bindings through the Odin objc intrinsics. The host polls
    `GCController.controllers` and reads `extendedGamepad`. The pinned Odin
    (dev-2026-08) has no `vendor:darwin/GameController`.
  - Windows: XInput. Open `xinput1_4.dll` with `LoadLibraryA` and get
    `XInputGetState` with `GetProcAddress`. Use the types from
    `core:sys/windows`, but not its foreign procs, which link
    `xinput.lib`. If the DLL does not load, log once and report no pads.
  - Linux: evdev through `core:sys/linux` syscalls. At startup, scan
    `/dev/input/event*` for `BTN_GAMEPAD`. Watch `/dev/input` with
    `inotify`. If an open fails with `EACCES`, try again for about 1 s,
    because udev sets the access rights after it makes the node. `xpad`
    reports X as 0x133 (`BTN_NORTH`) and Y as 0x134 (`BTN_WEST`), so the
    host reads each pad's driver name from sysfs and swaps the two codes
    for `xpad` only (decided 2026-10-26).
  - The XInput index is a device key, not the slot. The shared slot table
    assigns slots on every OS.
- Rejected: IOKit HID, raw HID input and a mapping database (each needs a
  table for each pad), `Windows.Gaming.Input` (WinRT and COM),
  GameInput (the player installs a runtime), `libudev` (a new library),
  and a newer Odin for `vendor:darwin/GameController` (a catalog entry and
  a compiler move for about ten selectors). Karl2D uses the same three
  OS interfaces, with `libudev` for hot-plug on Linux.
- Bridge: `step` gains `gamepads`, a list of
  `{ slot, held, tap, left_stick, right_stick, left_trigger,
  right_trigger }`. Missing fields are zero. While the Bridge is on, its
  pads replace the real pads. A request with no `gamepads` means no pad is
  connected. The `step` reply's held echo includes the pads.
- Tests: each backend has a pure mapping procedure from the OS state
  (an `XINPUT_STATE`, a list of evdev events, a snapshot of the GC
  values) to the host Gamepad state. Odin tests drive these procedures on
  every runner. The OS calls get a smoke test only: with no pad, the host
  reports an empty list and does not crash.
- Docs: ADR 0015 records the backends. `guide/gamepad.md` follows
  `input.md` and gives the position-to-label table, the limits on each OS
  and the Bridge fields. `guide/bridge.md` gains the `gamepads` field.
- Tutorial chapter 9: the left stick walks, with speed from how far the
  player pushes the stick. The keys still work: the chapter adds the stick
  to the key axes and clamps the result to the unit disc. `Start` quits.
  One short section explains `slot` and `Button.pressed_any`.
- Kula: `DpadUp` held or left stick y above 0.5 rolls forward. `DpadLeft`
  and `DpadRight` pressed turn. `South` pressed jumps. `Start` pressed
  quits. The stick does not turn.
- Release: v0.5.0. Tests start from `Input.empty`, so a later field costs
  them no edit.
- Manual check: the person has an Xbox pad, a Mac and a Windows machine.
  Linux is checked later on an Arch MacBook Air, with the pad on a cable.
  A bug found there goes into a v0.5.x patch.

## Out of scope

- Rumble, LEDs, gyro and the touchpad. Rumble comes first later, as a
  Command.
- The Guide button and button-prompt glyphs.
- Mouse buttons. These wait for pointer input (5rxq8tn7).
- Dead zone knobs in `Launch`.
- Pads beyond 4.

## Tasks in order

See the subtasks.

1. 1h9pnzrf: The gamepad Vocabulary change and the Bridge (first).
2. 4uhhgic9: macOS: GameController through dlopen (after 1).
3. gajxihcd: Windows: XInput through LoadLibraryA (after 1).
4. nzm56hlm: Linux: evdev and inotify (after 1).
5. 8d9n3z8z: Tutorial chapter 9, the gamepad guide and ADR 0015 (after 2,
   3 and 4).
6. gkgm6zf3: Cut v0.5.0 (after 5).
7. n6anliir: Kula: play with a gamepad, in the Kula repo (after 6).
8. xsl5lr4n: Check Linux with an Xbox pad (after 6; does not block the
   close).

Tasks 2, 3 and 4 can run in parallel.

name: The site renders the docs
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Parent

Milestone 18: docs and v0.2.0. Read it with `dex show f78a7omm --full`.

## What to build

This task's code lives in the `personal-site` repo
(`~/projects/personal-site`, Astro, deployed to pixelsprout.dev on Vercel).
Follow that repo's AGENTS.md, tests and smoke check.

1. A docs loader reads `guide/` from Pixelsprout/rocco-engine at the latest
   release tag, and downloads that release's `docs.tar.gz`. `DOCS_SOURCE`
   points it at a local checkout instead, as `DEX_SOURCE` does for the dex
   loader. A local preview with no release tarball shows the markers
   unchanged and says so in the build log.
2. The guide pages render at `/projects/rocco/docs/` and the chapters at
   `/projects/rocco/docs/tutorial/`, with a sidebar sorted by `order` in
   each folder. Relative links between pages and links to `images/` work as
   they do on GitHub.
3. The site replaces `{{platform_url}}`, `{{linalg_url}}`, `{{mesh_url}}`,
   `{{ui_url}}` and `{{roc_nightly}}` with the values in `urls.json`. An
   unknown marker fails the build.
4. The `roc docs` HTML is served at `/projects/rocco/api/`, with a small
   stylesheet override for the site's fonts and colours. The site does not
   parse that HTML.
5. The rocco project page links to the docs and the API.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover the loader's tag lookup, the `DOCS_SOURCE` path, the marker
  replacement and the unknown-marker failure.
- [ ] `pnpm run ci` passes in `personal-site`.
- [ ] A local build with `DOCS_SOURCE` set to a rocco-engine checkout shows
  `guide/install.md` and the API pages.
- [ ] Until the first release with `docs.tar.gz` exists, a production build
  still succeeds and the docs section says that no release has docs yet.

## Blocked by

- The docs step and the first page.
- Docs in the release.
result:
Done in personal-site, commits 0ce8538 and f1dc350 on main (pushed).

A docs loader reads the latest release from the GitHub API, reads guide/
at its tag through the git trees API and raw URLs, and unpacks its
docs.tar.gz. DOCS_SOURCE points it at a rocco-engine checkout: it reads
guide/ and build/docs/, leaves the markers unchanged and says so in the
build log. If the latest release has no docs.tar.gz, the build succeeds and
/projects/rocco/docs/ and /projects/rocco/api/ say that no release has docs
yet. A build against v0.1.0 showed this.

The guide renders at /projects/rocco/docs/<name>/ and the chapters at
/projects/rocco/docs/tutorial/<name>/, with a sidebar sorted by order in
each folder. The loader rewrites links before Astro renders the Markdown:
a page link goes to its route, a link to guide/images/ goes to the copied
file, and a link outside guide/ goes to the file on GitHub at the tag. The
urls.json markers are replaced, and any other text in double braces fails
the build.

The roc docs HTML is served unchanged at /projects/rocco/api/<package>/.
The loader appends src/styles/roc-docs.css (the site fonts and colours) to
each styles.css. An integration serves these files in dev and copies them
into dist/. The rocco project page links to ./docs and ./api.

Tests cover the tag lookup, the DOCS_SOURCE path, the marker replacement,
the unknown-marker failure, the link rewrite and the tar reader. The smoke
check builds against test/fixtures/rocco and test/fixtures/empty-docs.

Also in the diff: the GitHub fetch code moved from dex-source.ts to
github.ts, the prose styles moved into global.css, and headings site-wide
turn off ligatures (Pixelify Sans draws "fi" like an "A").

Known limits: a checkout preview links files outside guide/ to main; guide
folders after the top level sort by name; a page guide/tutorial.md would
clash with the tutorial folder index.

Note for g2vkmqcd: after v0.2.0 is published, check
pixelsprout.dev/projects/rocco/docs/ shows the pages with the markers
replaced.

name: Milestone 15: CI and the bundle
description:
Done when Kula builds on a clean machine with only Roc installed.

1. Three runners: macOS arm64, Ubuntu, Windows. Build the host, run the
examples headless, roc check and roc test every app.
2. Linux CRT objects and stubs committed. Windows import libraries from MinGW

4. Kula moves to its own repo on the bundle URL.

Part of 'The second arc' (docs/ROADMAP.md).

Decisions (grilled 2026-10-15):
- Kula moves to Pixelsprout/kula with its history (git filter-repo). games/
support leaves this repo. CI here runs cards, entity-game and pong.
- Pong is ported to the current seam and joins the all step.

name: Collision search limits the headline figure
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: research

In the reference run (bench/results/2026-10-21-intel-r-core-tm-i7-9700f-cpu-3-00ghz), the queries Span sets the headline. At mixed N=4,096 the median Frame budget is 11.5 ms, and queries is 3.2 ms per step, so 6.3 ms of it at 2 fixed steps. render_submit is 3.8 ms.

queries doubles each time N doubles, with only 8 raycasts, 8 overlaps and one ContactsOf: colliders goes from 34 us at N=64 to 15.5 ms at N=16,384. colliders-twin pays the same cost, so the cost is in the engine's collision search, not in Roc.

Question: does each Query test every Collider, or does the broadphase rebuild each step? What structure would make the Query cost grow slower than N?

Done when: the cause is known, and either a fix lands with a new colliders and mixed sweep, or a decision records why it stays.
result: Cause: Raycasts and Overlaps tested every Collider, ContactsOf ran a sweep on x (N sqrt N) over all Colliders, and each kind rebuilt the Shapes with an id map. Fixed in ce862f4 and 627d383: one shared ground-plane grid per step (ADR 0008). Check sweeps on the i7-9700F at 627d383: the queries Span at N=16,384 fell from 15.5 ms to 1.1 ms (colliders), and mixed p99 at N=8,192 is 12.8 ms, so the headline would move from 4,096 to 8,192 pending a new reference run. render_submit now leads the mixed Frame.

name: The 3D tree crosses the seam
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

ADR 0014, step 3. One change, no deprecated path.

- Add the nominal `Node` union to `platform/Vocabulary.roc`. Replace `draws`, `lights` and `colliders` with `nodes : List(Node)`.
- Add `Launch.capacity.groups`, default 1024.
- In the host, walk the tree with one recursive procedure.
- Pair Groups by Group id in their own map, sized at init. The first duplicate wins, and the host logs once.
- If a Node has the same parent Group id in both Scenes, interpolate its local Pose, then compose.
- If the parent changed, compose both world Poses, then interpolate.
- A Light takes its Group's interpolated Pose and its own local Pose from the current Scene.
- A Group moves a Point Light and turns a Directional dir. It does not change an Ambient.
- Take the Sun and the light cap in depth-first, pre-order walk order.
- Compose each Collider's world Pose from the current Scene before the host answers the Queries.
- Make the Bridge scene reply mirror the tree with local Poses: {"Group":{"pose":{...},"children":[...]}}.
- Move every game, bench game, tutorial chapter and guide page.
- In entity-game, put the drops in the player's Group. Delete the hand-written composition and World.yaw.
- Add a test: a drop on a turning Group follows an arc at alpha 0.5, not a chord.
- Add a test: a Node that changes parent interpolates in world space.
- Run the tracked host over a long Headless run of entity-game. Confirm no LEAK and no BAD Free.
result: Scene.nodes replaces draws, lights and colliders. Launch.capacity.groups defaults to 1024, at most 1048576. tree_walk in engine/scene_tree.odin walks the tree. Groups pair by Group id; the first duplicate wins and the host logs once. A Draw that leaves a duplicate Group does not pair (fixed in f5986e7). The Bridge scene reply mirrors the tree with local Poses and a Group id. entity-game puts the drops in the player's Group and has no World. Tests cover the arc at alpha 0.5 and a parent change in world space. A 20000-step tracked Headless run of entity-game shows no LEAK and no BAD Free. The tree walk adds about 8% to the interpolation median and about 9% to the queries median.

commit.message: perf(engine): Keep the tree walk near the cost of the flat Draw list

name: Kula: copy the idle bob
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: task

## What to build

The ball squashes and stretches about its up axis while it is not in a forward jump. games/kula/SPEC.md "Idle bob" states the rule.

- Ball keeps a bob phase in turns. Each step advances it by (165 - 1.25 * seconds left) * 50/4096 turns a second.
- The clone has no level clock yet. Until one exists, use 100 seconds left: one bob every 2.05 s.
- s = 0.0488 * sin(phase). View scales the ball by 1 + s across up and 1 - 2s along up. The axis is the ball's up, not a model axis.
- View moves the draw centre by -2s * radius along up. The ball's bottom then stays on the floor.
- The phase holds during a forward jump and during the edge wrap. The shape holds its last value.
- Leave the landing squish to 42fsutrf. Keep s separate so that task can add to it.

## Done when

- roc test covers the period at full clock, the peak scales and the floor contact.
- The bob plays in the running game.
- SPEC.md moves the idle bob out of "Not copied".
result: Ball.bob holds the phase. It runs at the full-clock rate, 2.05 s a bob, and holds in a forward jump, a fall arc and the edge wrap. View.ball_draw squashes along up through scale_rot and drops the centre by 2s*radius.

commit.message: feat(engine): Scale a Draw along scale_rot and copy the Kula idle bob - Draw gains scale_rot. The model is T * R * F * S * F^-1, and the host slerps F between Scenes. - The shader lights normals with the inverse transpose. engine/transform.odin is gone. - linalg adds Quat.conjugate and Quat.between. Every game sends Quat.identity for scale_rot. - Kula squashes the ball along up at the full-clock rate, 2.05 s a bob, and keeps it on the floor. - DESIGN.md, CONTEXT.md, SPEC.md and ADR 0002 record the scale frame and the bob.

name: Kula: jump in place and the forward-jump rules
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

The original has two kinds of jump. The clone has only the forward jump, and Space always starts it. Copy the original. See the Jump section of games/kula/SPEC.md, read from the decompilation 2026-10-13. Decided with the user 2026-10-13: copy the original on every open point.

## Requirements

Jump kinds:
1. Space while the ball is still and Up is not held starts a jump in place. The ball rises and lands on the same cell, with the same duration and peak as the forward jump. The pose does not change, apart from turns.
2. Space while Up is held starts a forward jump, as now.
3. Space during a floor roll starts a forward jump at once, from the ball's current position. Climbs and turns cannot start a jump. Changed with the user 2026-10-14: an edge roll can start a forward jump until the ball reaches the edge, as in the original (HandleViewportRotationStart). The jump starts from the roll's from cell.
   - The landing cell is two cells ahead of the cell the ball is nearest to: the roll's from cell when t < 0.5, else its target cell.
   - View moves the ball from its current interpolated position to the landing cell.
   - Keys collect on commit, so a key in the roll's target cell is already collected.
4. Bounces: a block above bounces both kinds. A block one or two cells ahead bounces only the forward jump. A bounced ball does not move, as now.

Mid-air input:
5. No input acts during a forward jump.
6. During a jump in place, Left and Right turn the ball. The turn takes 0.32 s and can outlast the jump. A turn press during a turn starts that turn when the current one ends (the original's startTurningLeftNextFrame).

Landing:
7. The landing check runs in the last 11 of 27 frames (t >= 16/27). The ball lands when its centre is at or below rest height over a floor. On level ground this is t = 1. Add an expect that shows the window.
8. If Up is held when a jump lands, the next roll starts in the same step, with no rest step. Use the same rule when a roll ends with Up held, which also fixes item 2 of 0v9t9lz3.

Docs:
9. Update the Clone column of the Jump table in SPEC.md and the Moves and Controls sections of games/kula/README.md.

## Not in scope

- The long jump, the Bouncy pill and bounce pads (SPEC.md, Long jump).
- The jump's height and frame count. They are in GGI data, not the C code.
- The sideways snap of AutoAlignJumpStartPos. The clone's ball is always on the cell line.

## Done when

- roc test games/kula/main.roc passes, with an expect for each requirement 1 to 8.
- By hand on arm64mac: Space alone hops in place, Up+Space jumps the level1 gap, Space mid-roll jumps at once, Left during a hop turns the ball, and held Up rolls without a pause through cells and after a landing.
result: Jump in place, forward-jump rules, mid-air turns with a turn queue, the landing window and held-Up roll chaining. Edge rolls can start a forward jump before the edge (changed with the user 2026-10-14). Checked by hand by the user.

name: Simplify the macOS sysroot script to keep the SDK layout
description:
Rewrite scripts/make-macos-sysroot.sh so that it copies SDK framework stubs with their real layout. Remove the re-export stripping and the objc.framework trick.

Why: the header of the script is wrong for Roc nightly-2026-09-12-220fd47. An LLD_REPRODUCE capture of 'roc build' shows that Roc passes -syslibroot platform/targets/macos-sysroot, -F <sysroot>/System/Library/Frameworks, -L <sysroot>/usr/lib and -lSystem. Re-exports failed only because the script writes a flat Foo.framework/Foo.tbd. lld resolves each re-export by its install name under the syslibroot, for example AppKit.framework/Versions/C/AppKit.tbd.

Evidence from the experiment:
- Sysroot = the Xcode SDK itself: the link fails. Roc emits one -framework per framework in the sysroot. QTKit and JavaNativeFoundation are Intel-only, SwiftUICore refuses clients, and Message does not resolve. So the script must still pick the frameworks.
- Sysroot = the 16-framework closure copied with 'cp -R -P' from the SDK (Versions/ and symlinks kept, nothing stripped), plus usr/lib/libSystem*.tbd and usr/lib/libobjc*.tbd, and no objc.framework: the link passes and bodies.bin runs. otool -L shows /usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib, linked through the Foundation re-export.

Steps:
1. Keep the closure walk over reexported-libraries. Re-exported frameworks must exist in the sysroot, or lld cannot resolve them.
2. For each framework in the closure, copy only the .tbd files and the symlinks that point to them: Foo.framework/Foo.tbd -> Versions/Current/Foo.tbd, Versions/Current -> <V>, and Versions/<V>/Foo.tbd. Do not copy Headers or Modules. A full 'cp -R -P' copy is 33 MB, mostly headers.
3. Copy usr/lib/libSystem.tbd, libSystem.B.tbd, libobjc.tbd and libobjc.A.tbd, with their symlinks.
4. Delete strip_reexports and the objc.framework block.
5. Rewrite the header comment. Keep one real constraint: Roc links every framework in the sysroot, so the sysroot holds only the frameworks the host needs.
6. Run 'roc scripts/build.roc -- all' from an empty platform/targets/macos-sysroot and run examples/bodies.

Done when examples/bodies links and runs with the new sysroot, 'otool -L examples/bodies/bodies.bin' lists /usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib, and the script has no stripping code.

Related: a Zulip question asks whether a platform header can name its frameworks. If Roc adds that, the sysroot can become the SDK path and this script can go.
result: Obsolete: iheupr8y replaced the script with a generated sysroot

name: Kula: convert Roll Away Hiro levels 1 to 3
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Kula plays Roll Away (USA) Hiro levels 1 to 3 in place of its own three
levels. Do this work in the Kula repo (Pixelsprout/kula), on the branch of
the rc move. See the milestone task for the decisions.

## What to build

- Add a Python script in `scripts/` that uses only the standard library. It
  takes the path of the disc image (`.bin`, MODE2/2352) and a level number.
  1. Read the ISO9660 file system from the raw sectors and find `HIRO.PAK`.
  2. Unpack the PAK: a file count, offset and size entries, names, then zlib
     data (wiki.kula.quest/archives/pak/).
  3. Parse the level: an i16 grid of 34x34x34 cells, index
     x*1156 + y*34 + z. -1 is empty, 0 plain, 1 fire, 2 ice, 3 invisible,
     4 acid, 5 or more points to a 256-byte record
     (wiki.kula.quest/levels/level/).
  4. Write Kula's text format.
- If the script finds a cell value, record type or object that Kula cannot
  show, it stops and names it. A `--list` flag prints every block type,
  record type and object a level uses, with counts.
- Extend the level format and `Level.roc`:
  - The layer grid stays for blocks.
  - A new section lists one item per line: `x y z face item`.
  - It also holds `start x y z face forward`.
  - The old item characters and `S` stay as shortcuts for the +y face and
    the default start.
- Map the original axes to Kula's: layer is y, row is z, column is x. Check
  the up axis against the decomp (`src/level_init.c`).
- Replace `levels/level1.txt` to `level3.txt` with Hiro levels 1 to 3. Use one
  Theme for all three.
- Credit "level layouts from Roll Away / Kula World (Game Design Sweden,
  1998)" in the README. Commit no other disc data.
- A test checks the block and item counts of the parsed grid against the
  text output.

## Done when

- `--list` output for Hiro levels 1 to 3 is in this task's result. The
  feature task uses it.
- The three levels parse, or the script names each feature Kula lacks.
result:

name: Emit non-recursive tag unions from the Odin glue
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Work in the roc-odin-glue repo (the glue/ submodule, also checked out at ~/playground/roc-odin-glue). Commit there, then bump the submodule here. The Zig glue is the reference: ~/playground/odin-game-engine/ZigGlue.roc (union emission about lines 900-1080).

Requirements:
- Emit a union with payloads as three types:
    <Name>_Tag :: enum uN { ... }
    <Name>_Payload :: struct #raw_union { <snake_tag>: T, ... }
    <Name> :: struct { payload: <Name>_Payload, _padN: [n]u8, tag: <Name>_Tag }
  Do not use Odin's union.
- Take the discriminant width from AbiLayout discriminant_size(). Take the tag values from the tu.tags order. Order multi-field payloads by payload_fields (alignment order), as the Zig glue does.
- Assert size, alignment and offset_of(tag) == discriminant_offset(Pointer64).
- Emit a union with no payloads as a bare enum uN, with no struct.
- Name a union by its field path, the same walk as records (for example Roc_View_Colliders_Shape). Use tu.name when it is present.
- Teach walk, reach and odin_type to follow RocTagUnion payloads.
- Crash with a clear message that names the type for a recursive union, and for a union payload that needs refcounting (List, Str, Box). release_proc must not silently treat such a union as Flat.
- Emit the 64-bit layout only. No accessors or constructors.
- Add a fixture glue/example/unions/ with one type per case: no payloads, one payload per tag, a multi-field payload, a nested union, a union in a record and a union in a list. check.sh diffs it against expected, builds it with -vet -strict-style, and runs an odin test that checks the layout.
- README: remove non-recursive tag unions from the unimplemented list. Keep recursive unions and refcounted union payloads on it.

Done when:
- glue/example/check.sh passes with the new fixture;
- the submodule bump here leaves engine/roc_platform_abi.odin unchanged (Collider has no union yet) and host-check passes.
result: OdinGlue emits non-recursive tag unions (glue 93aaaee): a tag enum, a payload raw union and a struct with the tag at its committed offset, or a bare enum for unions with no payloads. Anonymous unions take path names; the compiler names them by joining tags with Or, so only a := union keeps tu.name. Recursive, single-tag and refcounted-payload unions crash with the type's name. example/unions covers each case with a layout test. Engine glue is unchanged and host-check passes. roc glue caches by platform and can return an older spec's output; check.sh uses --no-cache.

commit.message: chore(glue): Bump roc-odin-glue to emit non-recursive tag unions

name: Parse .glb files into mesh data
description:
Write a GLB parser in Odin in engine/gltf.odin. Do not use vendor:cgltf.

- Read the GLB header, the JSON chunk (core:encoding/json), the BIN chunk and the accessors.
- Load positions, normals, indices and each primitive's material pbrMetallicRoughness.baseColorFactor. Write that colour into the vertex color. If a primitive has no material, use grey 0.8.
- Accept u8, u16 and u32 index accessors and convert them to u16. Reject a mesh with more than 65,535 vertices.
- Merge every triangle primitive of every mesh node into one mesh. Bake each node's world transform into positions and normals. Reject a primitive whose mode is not triangles.
- Do not flip winding.

Tests build GLB bytes in Odin test code. Cases: a good file, a bad magic number, missing normals, a non-triangle mode, a node transform, two primitives with different material colours.

name: render_submit limits the headline figure
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: research

In the reference run at e1eb378 (bench/results/2026-10-21-intel-r-core-tm-i7-9700f-cpu-3-00ghz), render_submit is the largest Span of the mixed Frame. At mixed N=8,192 it takes 7.1 ms of the 11.4 ms median Frame budget, and the p99 is 12.8 ms. At N=16,384 the p99 is 25.7 ms, over the 16.6 ms budget. The next largest Spans at N=8,192 are interpolation (1.0 ms), view (0.6 ms) and queries (0.6 ms, after ADR 0008).

render_submit grows in step with the Draws: draws costs about 0.82 to 0.87 us per Draw from N=1,024 to 16,384, and mixed costs about the same. The Span measures the CPU side only: the shadow pass and the Main pass with one draw call per Draw, the sky and the UI submit, without begin_pass (docs/BENCHMARKS.md, Spans).

Question: where do the 0.85 us per Draw go? For example, the uniform upload for each Draw, the two passes (shadow and Main) each issuing a draw call, or the sokol and D3D11 calls per draw. What would cut the cost per Draw, such as instancing, one uniform buffer update per pass, or merging Draws that share a Mesh?

Done when: the cause is known, and either a fix lands with a new draws and mixed sweep, or a decision records why it stays.

The target comes from Env.platform!: arm64mac, x64glibc or x64win. Other machines exit 1. The script also exits 1 when it is not run from the repo root.

Design: pure functions build every command and copy list (parse, target_for, host_run, game_run, glue_run, shaders_run, sokol_copies, compiler_rt_copy, windows_sdk_copies, newest_sdk). A thin effect layer runs them. Target carries an extra_inputs tag (MacSdk, WindowsSdk, BuiltInDocker), so inputs matches on the tag, not on the target name.

- macOS inputs: copies the 4 sokol Metal debug archives, copies libclang_rt.osx.a from 'xcrun clang -print-resource-dir'/lib/darwin, and runs scripts/make-macos-sysroot.sh. The sysroot step is extra: before, it was README step 0, and the game author needs it.

name: Roc heap A/B: allocation map against size header
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Parent

Milestone 16: Benchmarks (zbygy2an). Read it with `dex show zbygy2an --full`.

## What to build

A compile-time define, `ROCCO_ROC_HEAP`, chooses `map` or `header`. The header version stores each block's size in a header before the block. The header is at least 16 bytes and at least the alignment. Realloc reads the old size from the header and asks the backing allocator to resize, so a block can grow in place. The `live` counter is `allocs - deallocs` in both versions. Run a sweep with each version, record the result, then delete the losing version and the define.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One test suite calls roc_alloc, roc_dealloc and roc_realloc directly, and both versions pass it.
- [ ] The suite checks that realloc keeps the contents when a block grows and shrinks, that alignment holds and that the counters agree.
- [ ] `alloc-check.sh` passes with both versions.
- [ ] A sweep compares both versions on the Model size bench game. The summaries record the version and the realloc counts.
- [ ] The result is in the ticket's result. The losing version and the define are deleted.

## Blocked by

- cit5kurl
- zi6urdhv
result: A/B in 78ae3bd; header kept, map removed in f6a0422. Micro (-o:speed): alloc+free pair ~50 ns map vs ~15 ns header; 12 doubling reallocs 16 B to 64 KiB 1.7-2.0 us vs 0.98 us; 255 +16 B reallocs to 4 KiB 24-25 us vs 4.6 us. Model size sweep does 2 allocs, 0 reallocs per step: header faster at N<=512 (0.21 vs 0.12 us at N=64), equal within noise above. Sweep was noisy (other agents running). Raw data was in the implementer's scratchpad, not committed.

commit.message: merge: Roc heap A/B: allocation map against size header (usauwcfh)

name: Kula Themes and level progression
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

## Parent

nc3cv6do (Milestone 12: packs, textures and PBR). Read its spec first.

## What to build

Kula plays three levels, each in its own Theme, swapping packs between them. A kula pack, loaded from init, holds the ball and shared assets. A Theme record holds its pack name, asset names, lights and sun direction; a table in Kula code maps each level to its Theme. Finishing level N sends Load for Theme N+1; on loaded Kula switches its ids and starts the level after a short pause; the next step sends Unload for the old pack. Finishing level 3 keeps Won. Levels 2 and 3 are hand-written .txt files in the existing format. Themes differ by tint and lights for now; textures come in the Kula look ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Roc expects: the Theme table covers three levels; finishing a level returns Load for the next pack; loaded switches ids; the next step returns Unload for the old pack; level 3 ends in Won.
- [ ] Levels 2 and 3 parse and are finishable.
- [ ] By eye: playing through shows three Themes and no magenta.

## Blocked by

- 7zk6yajs
result: Theme.roc maps levels 1-3 to haze, inca, arctic (pack, assets, sun, lights, tint). Clearing a level sends Load for the next Theme; loaded switches the face id and starts the level after a 1 s Starting pause; the next step sends Unload for the old Theme. Level 3 ends in Won. Each Theme pack names the shared face for now; bfn69njy gives each Theme its own faces. Real host checked with forced exits: haze, inca, arctic swap and unload, no id 0.

commit.message: feat(kula): Play three levels, each in its own Theme pack - Theme.roc maps each level to a Theme: pack, assets, sun, lights and block tint. - init loads the kula pack (ball) and the level 1 Theme. Expects play each route to its exit. Level 3 ends in Won. - A fall restarts the current level.

1. Create packages/ui/ beside packages/camera/ and packages/mesh/.
2. box(config, children) gives [Open(config)] ++ children ++ [Close]. text(str, style) gives one Text.
3. A default Box config with Clay's defaults: Fit sizing, Start alignment, Row, zero padding and gap, transparent background, no float.
4. Helpers for common cases, such as float_at(LeftTop, offset), if they stay small.

## Done when
- Roc expect tests show nested helpers give the right stream.
- The full suite passes.
result: packages/ui/ gives Ui.box, Ui.text, default_box, float_at and pad_all. Roc expect tests check nested streams. A Scene with ui: Ui.box(...) type-checks.

commit.message: feat(ui): Add packages/ui to build the UI stream - box(config, children) gives Open, the flattened child streams, then Close. - text(str, style) gives a one-item stream, so boxes and text mix in one child list. - default_box holds Clay's defaults. float_at and pad_all cover common configs. - Roc expect tests check nested streams. README lists the package.

name: Milestone 14: the HUD
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Done when the key count changes on screen without a 3D draw. A box that floats to a corner stays there when the window resizes, and the count reads right at two window sizes.

Decided in the Milestone 14 grilling on 2026-10-15. ADR 0004 records "UI layout runs in the host". CONTEXT.md defines UI, Element, Box, Text and Rgba.

## Problem Statement

A game can draw only meshes in 3D. It cannot put a number, a word or a panel flat on the screen. Kula needs to show the keys collected. Later games need menus and inventories with nested layouts.

## Solution

Scene gains ui : List(Element), a flat stream of Open(Box), Text and Close. The host feeds the stream to C Clay once per frame, against the window size. The host measures text with one baked SDF font and draws Clay's render commands as one batch of quads inside the Main pass. Games write nested code with packages/ui/, which builds the stream. Kula shows "Keys 1 / 2" in a panel at the top-left.

## User Stories

1. As a game author, I want to put text and boxes on screen from view, so that my UI is a Description like my Draws.
2. As a game author, I want to write nested boxes in Roc, so that I do not write Open and Close by hand.
3. As a game author, I want to anchor a box to a corner of the window, so that it stays there when the window resizes.
4. As a game author, I want Clay's sizing (Fit, Grow, Fixed, Percent), padding, gap, direction and child alignment, so that my layouts can grow past a key count.
5. As a game author, I want a background colour with alpha and a corner radius, so that a panel can sit over the 3D view.
6. As a game author, I want Text at any size and colour, so that I do not choose from fixed font sizes.
7. As a game author, I want an empty Box config to mean what Clay means, so that defaults do not surprise me.
8. As a game author, I want unbalanced Open and Close to log once and still draw, so that a bug is visible, not fatal.
9. As a game author, I want a character the font does not have to draw as "?" and log once, so that I see the gap.
10. As a player, I want the UI drawn sharp and at its authored colour, so that the tone map does not change it.
11. As a Kula player, I want to see the keys collected out of the total, so that I know how many are left.
12. As an engine maintainer, I want Clay pinned as a submodule and copied by the inputs step, so that updates are one command.
13. As an engine maintainer, I want the font baked by a build step into a committed Odin file, so that the build needs no font tool.
14. As an engine maintainer, I want no allocation per frame for the UI, so that the frame cost stays fixed.
15. As an engine maintainer, I want the corner anchor tested at two window sizes through Frame_Render's capture, so that the milestone check is automatic.

## Implementation Decisions

Vocabulary:
- Rgba : { r, g, b, a }, linear channels from 0 to 1, alpha not premultiplied. Tint stays Rgb.
- Element : [Open(Box), Text(Text), Close]. The union is not recursive, so the glue carries it. An Element's identity is its place in the list.
- Box: width and height as [Fit({ min, max }), Grow({ min, max }), Fixed(F32), Percent(F32)], pad { left, right, top, bottom }, gap, direction [Row, Col], child_align { x, y } as [Start, Center, End], background : Rgba, radius : F32 (one value), floating [NoFloat, Float({ attach : AttachPoint, offset })]. AttachPoint has Clay's nine names, LeftTop to RightBottom. A Box floats to the window root only.
- Text: the string, size, color : Rgba, wrap [Words, None].
- Names and defaults follow Clay (Fit, Start), so an empty config means the same on both sides.
- Scene gains ui : List(Element). Every game adds ui: [], except pong (ntbh6adj).
- The game does not learn the window size. Sizes are logical pixels. The host multiplies by sapp.dpi_scale(), which is 1 while high_dpi is off.
- The UI is a Description. The host draws the current Scene's UI only, with no interpolation.

Host:
- Clay enters as a git submodule pinned to a commit. The inputs step copies its prebuilt lib from bindings/odin/clay-odin/ per target, like sokol's. platform/main.roc lists it per target. arm64mac and x64glibc only. If a prebuilt lib fails on a target, compile clay.h for that target in the inputs step.
- The Clay arena comes from perm at init, sized by MinMemorySize() with the default element cap.
- The host lays out once per frame against sapp.width() and sapp.height(), from the current Scene. It walks the stream in order: Open calls open and configure, Text adds text, Close closes.
- A Close with no open Box is ignored. Boxes still open at the end are closed. Each logs once.
- A Clay error logs once per kind and the host draws what fits.
- Text strings point into the current Scene, which lives for the frame, so the host copies no string.
- The measure callback uses the baked metrics. One font, so the font id is always 0.
- A character outside ASCII 32 to 126 draws as "?" and logs once.

Drawing:
- The UI draws inside the Main pass, after the sky, with its own pipeline: no depth test, no depth write, alpha blend, sample count 4.
- Every rectangle and glyph goes into one dynamic vertex buffer per frame, sized at init (about 16k quads). One draw call per scissor or texture change. Past the cap, the host drops the rest and logs once.
- A new ui program in engine/shaders/basic.glsl draws rounded rectangles and SDF glyphs with smoothstep. Colours are linear, skip the tone map, and go through the sRGB encode, like the sky.
- Frame_Render owns the UI pass, and its capture adapter records the quads.

Font:
- One SDF atlas, ASCII 32 to 126, from Atkinson Hyperlegible (OFL). The .ttf and its licence are committed under scripts/fonts/.
- A Font step in scripts/build.roc runs an Odin bake tool that uses vendor:stb/truetype (stbtt_GetCodepointSDF). It writes engine/font_baked.odin with a "Generated, do not edit" header. If the tool cannot run, the committed file stays, as for shader_basic.odin.

packages/ui/:
- Nested helpers such as box(config, children) and text(str, style) flatten to the Element stream.
- A default Box config with Clay's defaults.

Kula:
- Hud.roc builds the UI: a Box floating at LeftTop with offset 16, background Rgba with a = 0.5, radius 8. Inside it, Text "Keys n / total" at size 24 in white. n is collected.len() and total is keys_left + collected.len().
- The HUD shows in every phase. No level number and no win banner.
- The README gains "keys collected". The word "held" stays for Input.

## Testing Decisions

- The corner anchor is tested through Frame_Render's capture with a fake game's Scene: a box floating at RightBottom, checked at two window sizes.
- Stream errors are tested through the same seam: an unbalanced Open, an extra Close and the quad cap, each logged once.
- The font measure is a plain procedure, tested against known metrics, including the "?" fallback.
- packages/ui/ is tested with Roc expect: nested helpers give the right stream.
- Kula is tested with Roc expect: Hud gives "Keys 1 / 2" after one key is collected.
- The shader and blending are checked by eye: scripts/screenshot.sh kula at 960x540 and at a second size.
- The Linux container run exits 0.
- The full suite runs once at the end of each task: odin test engine, host-check.sh, each game's roc test and the build script tests.

## Out of Scope

- high_dpi (follow-up task).
- Pointer input, hover and clicks (follow-up task; reopens ADR 0004).
- Images in a Box, borders, per-corner radius, scroll, clip, z-index, floating to another element, letter spacing and line height.
- Fonts that a game provides (kf5vd0lp).
- Window size and title in Config (z851lo4y).
- Pong (ntbh6adj) and the x64win target (Milestone 15).

## Further Notes

- Part of 'The second arc' (docs/ROADMAP.md).
- terrocotta (github.com/obust/terrocotta) ports Clay to Roc. We copied its vocabulary and its open/close stream, not its solver.
- Order: (1) docs, (2) Clay link, (3) vocabulary, (4) font, (5) UI pass, (6) packages/ui, (7) Kula HUD. Steps 3 and 4 are independent. Step 5 needs 2, 3 and 4.
result: Kula shows the keys collected through Scene.ui, Clay in the host and packages/ui. See the Milestone 14 results in docs/ROADMAP.md.

commit.message: feat(kula): Show the keys collected in a HUD - Hud.ui builds a panel floating at the top-left with "Keys n / total" at size 24 in white. - view sets Scene.ui from Hud in every phase. - Roc expects check "Keys 0 / 2" at the start and "Keys 1 / 2" after one key. - The README describes the panel. The ROADMAP marks Milestone 14 done.

name: Link examples/cards end to end on the generic platform
description:
Write the new platform/main.roc from docs/DESIGN.md section 4 with Scene.camera, plus the drop_model_for_host export. Implement the call protocol in docs/DESIGN.md section 5 under the refcount-1 axiom. Call view once after init.

Host side of Config: seed from ROCCO_SEED (default 0), manifest with cube, sphere, slab as ids 1 to 3, built with the glue helpers through roc_alloc.

Host side of Input: the latch. A key down event adds the key to a pending set. The first fixed step of a frame takes it as pressed, plus the mouse delta. Later steps get an empty pressed and zero delta. held is the key state at the step. Empty lists allocate nothing. The host filters no keys.

name: macOS: wired Xbox One pads through GIP over IOKit USB
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

macOS reads wired Xbox One pads by speaking GIP over IOKit USB, beside the
GameController reader. Agreed on 2026-10-26 as a follow-up to PR #12.
Start from the result of the GIP probe task.

## Decisions so far

- Use Apple's IOKit USB API, opened with `dlopen`, with our own bindings.
  The macOS catalog gets no new entry. Do not use libusb, because a player
  would need Homebrew.
- The GameController reader keeps Bluetooth Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro
  and MFi pads. The GIP reader adds wired Xbox One pads. Both feed the same
  `[]Gamepad_Raw`, with ids that cannot collide.
- Put the GIP report parser in a file with no OS suffix, so every runner
  tests it. Odin tests drive it with reports captured from the probe.
- Amend ADR 0015. GIP is one protocol for every Xbox One pad, so the
  mapping-table reason for rejecting IOKit HID does not apply. Remove the
  wired Xbox One limit from `guide/gamepad.md`.

## Decided on 2026-10-26

- Hot-plug: rescan the matching USB devices once per second, as the Windows
  and Linux readers do. No IOKit notifications and no run-loop source.
- Match any interface with class ff, subclass 47 and protocol d0, not a
  fixed vendor and product. Send power on to every pad. Send the PDP LED
  and auth packets only to vendor 0x0e6f, as xpad does.
- Skip vendor 0x045e (Microsoft), so GameController keeps the official
  pads and no pad shows up twice. Whether GameController reads an official
  pad on a cable is untested; the guide says so.
- If a device fails to open, configure or start, log once for that device
  and skip it until it reconnects.

## Done when

The person plays chapter 9 and Kula on macOS with the PDP Afterglow on a
cable. The mapping tests pass on every runner, and the macOS catalog audit
shows no new symbol.

Facts: the result of g8b8n6tt (the GIP probe) gives the endpoints, start packets, report layout and IOKit steps.
result: Merged in PR #13. engine/gamepad_gip_darwin.odin reads wired Xbox One pads through GIP over IOKit USB, opened with dlopen, with no new catalog entry. The parser in engine/gamepad_gip.odin has 19 tests. The person played chapter 9 on macOS with the PDP Afterglow on a cable. Fixed during the check: a pad gives a new client the reports the last client did not read, so the reader lists a pad 100 ms after the open and its first poll drops the tap latch. ROCCO_NO_GAMEPADS=1 lets the alloc check run with a pad plugged in. Kula with the pad stays in n6anliir.

name: Milestone 22: the 3D tree
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

The Scene carries `draws`, `colliders` and `lights` as flat lists in world
space. It does not show what belongs to what. `examples/entity-game` keeps
parenting in the game (Milestone 5). Its `view` composes each world pose by
hand for Draws, Colliders and Lights, and keeps a separate `World.yaw`
because a Collider turns by yaw only. The host lerps world positions, so a
drop on a turning player takes a chord, not an arc.

## Solution

The 3D Scene crosses the seam as a tree:
`Node := [Group({ id, pos, rot }, List(Node)), Draw(Draw), Light(Light), Collider(Collider)]`.
`Scene.nodes` replaces `draws`, `lights` and `colliders` in one change.
A Group carries a Group id and a Pose with no scale. The host interpolates
in local space and composes. ADR 0014 (proposed) records every decision.
`CONTEXT.md` defines Node, Group, Group id and Pose.

Done when:
- A Collider turns by `rot : Quat`, and `bench/colliders` records the time
  before and after the general box test.
- `packages/linalg` has `Pose.compose` and `Pose.relative`.
- Every game, bench game, tutorial chapter and guide page writes
  `Scene.nodes`. No `draws`, `lights` or `colliders` field remains.
- entity-game parents its drops with a Group and has no hand-written
  composition and no `World.yaw`.
- The alloc check records entity-game's allocs per step. It has no target.
- ADR 0014 is accepted.
result: The 3D Scene crosses the seam as a tree of Nodes (PR #9). A Collider turns by a Quat. packages/linalg has Pose.compose and Pose.relative. Every game, bench game, tutorial chapter and guide page writes Scene.nodes. entity-game parents its drops with a Group. ADR 0014 is accepted.

name: A Quit from init does not stop a windowed run
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

## Problem

A `Quit` that `init` returns does not stop a windowed run. `seam_init` runs
init's Commands before `sapp.run` (engine/app.odin). `app_run_command` calls
`sapp.request_quit()`, which only sets `_sapp.quit_requested`. Then
`sapp_run` calls `_sapp_init_state`, which clears the whole `_sapp` struct
(sokol_app.h, `_SAPP_CLEAR_ARC_STRUCT`). The quit is lost and the window
opens. Headless honours it, because it sets `g_state.quit`.

A game that rejects its Args cannot stop from `init`. ADR 0007 says it does
so from `init` with `Quit`.

## What to build

Make a `Quit` from `init` stop the run before the window opens, on every
target. Keep the `Frame Count` line and exit code 0.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An engine test shows that a `Quit` from `init` stops a windowed run.
- [ ] guide/launch.md and guide/calls.md no longer say that a `Quit` from
  `init` stops only a Headless run.

Found by the review of the guide pages (34w71prh).

name: Kula Ball and View: rolls, turns, climbs, edge rolls, jumps, camera follows
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

The ball rolls, turns, climbs, rolls round edges and jumps, and the camera
follows. See the decisions in Milestone 10 (72omk38x). Grilled 2026-10-13.

## Requirements

Ball.roc:
1. `Ball : { pose : Pose, motion : Motion, rot : Quat }` with `Motion :
[Still, Rolling({ from : Pose, t : F32 }), Turning({ from : Pose, t : F32 }),
Jumping({ from : Pose, t : F32 })]`. Add Falling in the Rules ticket.
2. The pose commits when a move starts. `from` and `t` exist for View only.
Input is read only when Still.
3. `roll : Set(Cell), Pose -> Try(Pose, [ClosedEdge])` checks three cases
in order:
   a. Block at cell + forward: climb. cell stays, up' = -forward,
   forward' = up.
   b. Block at cell + forward - up: floor. cell' = cell + forward.
   c. Else: edge. cell' = cell + forward - up, up' = forward, forward' = -up.
   Case c needs an open end: Err(ClosedEdge) when a block sits left or
   right of the block at cell - up, as in the original.
   One expect per case. Case c is the milestone check.
4. `turn_left` and `turn_right` rotate forward a quarter turn about up with
Grid.cross. One expect each.
5. `jump : Set(Cell), Pose -> [Land(Pose), Fall(Pose), Bounce]`. Bounce when
a block sits at cell + up, cell + forward or cell + 2 forward. Land at
cell + 2 forward when a block sits at cell + 2 forward - up. Otherwise Fall
at cell + 2 forward. A jump never lands on the block ahead; the original
only climbs by rolling. Expects cover each outcome.
6. Timing from the original's PAL frame counts: a floor roll takes 0.26 s,
a climb 0.28 s, an edge roll 0.34 s, a turn 0.32 s, a jump 0.54 s. `advance : Ball,
F32 -> Ball` moves t and returns Still when t reaches 1.
7. Input: Up held starts the next roll on the step the current motion ends.
Left and Right act on press only. Space on press jumps. Key codes from
pf.Key; the binding lives in main.roc.
8. rot accumulates each step while Rolling: axis = cross(up, forward), angle
= distance / radius with radius 0.195, through Quat.mul. The distance is 1
for a floor roll, 2 (0.5 - radius) for a climb and 1 + radius pi / 2 for an
edge roll. A jump does not spin.

View.roc:
9. `interpolated : Ball -> { pos : Vec3, up : Vec3, forward : Vec3 }` lerps
from `from` to `pose` by t with Vec3.lerp; up and forward are normalised. A
jump adds a parabola of height 0.5 along up.
10. The ball's draw centre is pos - (0.5 - radius) up, scale 2 radius, with
rot. The centre rests 0.195 cell above the face. Round an edge the centre
goes half a cell to the edge, a quarter circle of one radius about the edge
line, then half a cell down the side, so the ball never enters the block.
11. Camera: the original's view space. The basis is the ball's frame pitched
down 250/4096 of a turn. The ball centre sits 250/512 below the view axis at
a depth of 800/512. vFOV 1.286 rad. No smoothing, no clipping test. After a
climb the eye sits inside the floor the ball left.
11a. Blocks draw as exposed faces: one primitive plane per face that borders
an empty cell. No face between two blocks. The one-sided planes are why the
floor does not hide the ball after a climb.
Changed 2026-10-13 from a fixed offset; see games/kula/SPEC.md.

main.roc:
12. step runs stages in order: read input, advance motion, (rules later),
then returns commands. Each stage is a function Model -> Model.
13. Model gains the Ball. init builds it from Level.start.

## Not in scope

- No keys, exit, win or falling. Fall returns a Pose and nothing acts on it
yet.
- No .glb meshes.

## Done when

- `roc test games/kula/main.roc` passes, with expects for the three roll
cases, both turns, every jump outcome, the timing and rot accumulation.
- By hand on arm64mac: the ball rolls over an edge onto the side of a block
and keeps rolling, and the camera follows round the edge.
result: Ball rolls, climbs, wraps edges and jumps two cells; the camera and block faces follow the original's numbers in games/kula/SPEC.md. Checked by hand on arm64mac.

commit.message: fix(kula): Hide faces within 1.12 cells of the eye

name: Choose the tone map per game
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: grilling

Today the shader applies one fixed ACES fit (65wor4ep, no knob). AgX keeps saturated highlights from shifting hue. Khronos PBR Neutral keeps material colours closest to their authored values. A game could choose one.

Config goes from the host to the game, so it cannot carry the choice. Options:
1. A Scene field, such as tone_map : [Aces, AgX, Neutral]. A Theme can change it per level.
2. A one-time Command at start-up.

Recommendation: a Scene field. Lights are already Scene data. Fog (s1zhf2hf) also wants a Scene field. Consider one Scene record for the look, such as exposure, tone map and fog, so Scene does not gain one field for each effect.

The host passes an int in fs_params and the fragment shader branches on it.

Decide once Themes exist and a scene shows ACES looking wrong. See games/kula/SPEC.md (Look).

name: Loops: pair Scene.loops by Loop id
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

See the milestone nmpfj41t and ADR 0012. After the Play task.

## What to build

After each `view`, the host pairs `Scene.loops` with the Loops of the
previous Scene by Loop id:
- A new Loop id starts a repeating voice.
- A missing Loop id stops its voice with a short fade of a few
  milliseconds, so there is no click.
- A changed gain, pitch or place applies at once.
- A changed Sound id restarts the voice from the start.
- If no voice is free, a new Loop waits silent and logs once. It starts
  when a voice frees and it is still in the Scene.
- Two Loops with the same id in one Scene: keep the first and log once.

## Done when

- Host tests cover start, stop, change, restart, a duplicate id and a Loop
  that waits for a voice. The tests use the engine with no device.
- A test reads mixed frames and finds that a stopped Loop goes to silence.
result: engine/loop.odin pairs Scene.loops with the Loops of the previous Scene by Loop id after each view. A new id starts a repeating voice; a missing id stops with a 5 ms fade; a changed gain, pitch or Place applies to the same voice; a changed Sound id restarts from the start. A new Loop with no free voice waits silent, logs once and starts when a voice frees. A duplicate id keeps the first and logs once. A Loop owns its voice only while the voice's take count matches, so Unload or a Play steal is detected. engine/loop_test.odin covers start, stop to silence in mixed frames, change, restart, a duplicate id, a waiting Loop and Unload, all on an engine with no device. Verified on macOS (369 host tests).

commit.message: feat(audio): Pair Scene.loops by Loop id

name: Game-level engine settings
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: grilling

Nothing goes from the game to the host at start-up. Config goes the other way.
Settings come in two kinds:
1. Start-up settings set GPU resources and cannot change per frame: shadow map
size, shadow bias, soft-shadow mode (PCF or PCSS), cascade count. A project
file such as games/<game>/rocco.toml fits them. The host reads it before init.
2. Look settings can change per level: tone map, fog, exposure. One Scene
record fits them.

Decide both homes in one grilling. Related: yjtqgdd4 (tone map), s1zhf2hf
(fog). Milestone 13 (cxtqbqrl) uses host constants until this lands.

Milestone 13 result: the Kula shadow edge looks a little soft. The edge width
comes from SHADOW_MAP_SIZE over the size of the box around the level, and from
the 3x3 PCF kernel. Expose both, so a game can trade sharpness for cost.
result:
The start-up half landed in Milestone 17 (nm2ai3l5, ADR 0007). A fifth call, launch : Config -> Launch, runs before init and before the window opens. Launch carries the window, step_hz, shadow_map and the capacities, so a game can trade shadow sharpness for GPU cost through shadow_map. The project file was rejected: it moves the decision out of Roc, it cannot read the Args, and roc test cannot see it. The cascade count stays an engine constant (75ah1rr3).

The look half lives in yjtqgdd4 (tone map) and s1zhf2hf (fog). The shadow biases, the normal offset and the PCF kernel or PCSS are shader knobs that can change per level, so they go to the same Look record.
